title: feat(pocket): 2D Pocket runs on the path kernel behind the planner switch
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

The first recipe on the path kernel (K6 of #4023): the 2D Pocket runs on the kernel when the planner switch is `new`. With the default switch (`old`) the old pocket planner runs, unchanged.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3752#issuecomment-7211302888

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_pocket.rs` (new): the 2D Pocket recipe. It maps the op parameters to one choice for each stage. It plans each Z level with the heights of that level, and the converter (`kernel_emit::emit_levels`) makes the level plans into one toolpath.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_level.rs` (new): `plan_level`, the stages of one level in the order of the record (guide, order, load, then link and entry for each cut, then the exit). It is not specific to the pocket. The fallbacks and the notes of the stages go to the status line.
- `crates/app/src/operation/planner_switch.rs`: `KERNEL_KINDS = [Pocket]`. Under `new`, `check_engine` lets the 2D Pocket through. Each other phase-1 kind is still refused by name.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs`, `generate.rs`: `run_job_on(job, engine)` and `generate_on(world, op, name, engine)`. `run_job` passes the one reading of the process setting (`planner_engine()`). The Pocket arm reads the engine that it gets and calls `pocket_on_kernel` under `new`.
- `crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`: `GenerateOperation::new_on(world, name, engine)`, the test hook of #4055 for the real command path.
- `crates/app/src/operation/pocket_kernel.rs` (new): the refusals by name under `new` for the options that this recipe does not plan.
- `crates/motion/src/kernel_emit/` (`mod.rs`, `pen.rs`): `LevelPlan::top_z`, the proved material top of a level (`None` is the stock top). The converter still refuses an approach under it (`APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`) and a level top above the stock top (`BAD_LEVEL_TOP`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_region.rs`: `without_slivers` (the stock less the fig8 band left a loop with all its points on one line, and the selection refused it).
- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/kind_pocket.rs` (new), `registry.rs`: the 2D Pocket row is `Moved`, with the real stage planners and the Waterline choices of the pocket.
- `docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`: the decisions.

## In scope and out of scope

What a 2D Pocket does under `CAMCRAFT_PLANNER=new`:

| Strategy | Under `new` |
|---|---|
| Waterline | Kernel: rings of the boundary at the stepover, load control `None` (each cut above the stated load is named), rings linked at depth, each lift named |
| Offset rings | Kernel: rings at the load step, `ConstantEngagement` with `Reach::Rings` (passes inserted where a ring cuts above the load) |
| Zigzag | Refused by name (`KERNEL_POCKET_ZIGZAG`, points to #3753) |
| Auto | The old rule: Waterline for a round outline (kernel), else Zigzag (refused by name, the text says that Auto chose Zigzag) |
| Adaptive | Refused by name (`KERNEL_POCKET_ADAPTIVE`; the old arm refuses it too) |

Also refused by name under `new`: rest machining (#3753), "do not touch" areas (#3754), the corner relief. 3D levels are the 3D Pocket kind, which `check_engine` still refuses under `new`. No silent fallback to the old planner.

The entry: a selected Helix or Ramp is used where the tool must enter material. Plunge asks for an entry outside material (an arc lead in air, a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column). A closed pocket with none of them is refused with `NO_SAFE_ENTRY` and its fix text.

## Old against new (law measures, #4154)

The disc of #3934 and the dog bone of #3741 in the 80 x 50 stock, tool radius 4, one level. Old: the pinned table of `laws_pockets::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_old_planner` (Auto). New: `k6_pocket::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_kernel` (Waterline on the kernel).

| Case | Planner | Lifts (named) | Crossings | Feeds out of reach | Entries: air / column / solid | Over the limit (worst deg) | Full width | Fallback notes | Laws broken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| disc Inside | old | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 18 (9 plunge, 9 helix) | 20 (178) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| disc Inside | new | 4 (4) | 1 | 6 | 2 / 2 / 1 (1 ramp) | 1205 (173) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| disc Outside | old | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 18 (9 plunge, 9 helix) | 20 (178) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| disc Outside | new | 5 (5) | 0 | 10 | 2 / 0 / 4 (4 ramp) | 362 (180) | 172 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| dog bone Inside | old | 26 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 26 (13 plunge, 13 helix) | 32 (180) | 1 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| dog bone Inside | new | 10 (10) | 1 | 6 | 2 / 8 / 1 (1 ramp) | 812 (173) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| dog bone Outside | old | 26 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 26 (13 plunge, 13 helix) | 32 (180) | 1 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| dog bone Outside | new | 9 (9) | 0 | 2 | 2 / 0 / 8 (8 ramp) | 310 (180) | 103 | 0 | link L4 L6 |

`testdata/models/fig8.step` (EM-0800-4FL, Outside containment, Waterline, stepover 3, stepdown 10, Helix; 3 levels). Old and new on the same op, read by `kernel_route::fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (heavy) and its light twin:

| Start | Planner | Moves | Lifts (named) | Crossings | Entries: air / column / solid | Over the limit (worst deg) | Full width | Laws broken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto | old | 2780 | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 / 3 / 18 (18 helix) | 1236 (180) | 183 | link L6 |
| Auto | new | 27996 | 18 (18) | 6 | 6 / 0 / 15 (15 ramp) | 8595 (180) | 4179 | link L4 L6 |
| Inside | old | - | 24 (0) | 0 | 0 / 24 / 3 (3 helix) | 1521 (180) | 339 | link L6 |
| Inside | new | refused by name (#4324: the order stage cannot restart a ring and keep its circle and lead) | | | | | | |
| Outside | old | 7573 | 96 (0) | 0 | 0 / 3 / 96 (96 helix) | 85 (135) | 0 | link L6 |
| Outside | new | 27996 | 18 (18) | 6 | 6 / 0 / 15 (15 ramp) | 8595 (180) | 4179 | link L4 L6 |

On fig8 the kernel's Auto resolves to Outside (the band reaches the stock edge with air beyond it), so the two rows are the same path. The fig8 spec of the meter has no part outline (the stock box only), so the meter does not judge the part walls here; the verifier does.

The open items, named and not hidden:
- #4260 and #4272: the full-width reads on Outside (172 and 103) are at the stock edge and on the approach of a stay link. The load stage and the #4154 meter read them differently.
- #4300: a feed of the plan crosses the arc lead of an entry. On the disc Inside and the dog bone Inside it is 1 crossing each (move 11 is in the arc lead of the first entry). On fig8 it is 6 (2 on each level): after a lift, the arc lead of the next air entry runs in from the air across the two outer rings cut before it. `Crossing` blocks the post, so the fig8 pocket does not post under `new` yet. The lead runs in stock that the rings cleared before (no gouge). I added this case to #4300.
- #4324 (new): the order stage refuses the fig8 pocket on the Inside start by name.
- Full width and over the limit on fig8 (4179 and 8595 against 183 and 1236): the same class as #4260 and #4272 (the full-width reads at the stock edge on the Outside start), with no load control (Waterline). The kernel path has about 10 times the moves of the old one (chords, not arcs), so the counts are not one to one. This is the largest open item of the recipe.
- "Over the limit": Waterline has no load control by design. The kernel names each read above the stated load (stepover / D) in one status line note. The meter counts each feed move, and the kernel rings are chords, so the count is higher than the old count of arc moves. The worst angle is the same or lower.
- The entries "solid ... ramp": the helix of the entry stage is chords (#4269 decision 5), so the meter reads it as a ramp. That gives the L4 mark (helix asked, ramp read, no fallback note). The entry stage did fly a helix.
- "Feeds out of reach": the arc leads of the air entries (#4254, #4269).
- #4236 (the chain region of a trace) is not reached by this recipe: the 2D Pocket region is a planar region.

## The verifier

On fig8 (app, through the real generate path): no `Gouge`, `RapidInStock`, `RapidInPart` or `PlungeIntoStock`. `FluteShort` and `ShankHit` are on the old path too (the 20 mm flute of EM-0800-4FL is short for the 20.5 mm pocket). The kernel adds 6 `Crossing` findings (#4300), and the post is blocked by them, as the rule says.

`k6_pocket::the_verifier_passes_each_kernel_pocket` runs the verifier of `camcraft-sim` on each kernel pocket of the pins (square pocket and pocket with a round island, Waterline and Offset rings, Auto / Inside / Outside; disc and dog bone, Auto / Inside / Outside). No `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock`, no `Gouge`. The findings that it reports: `Crossing` on the disc Inside and on the dog bone Inside (#4300). On the closed pockets the kernel has no more crossings than the old planner (0 and 0). The Zigzag trial (not in this PR) gave 30 and 48 `Crossing` findings against 0 for the old planner: that is why Zigzag is refused.

## Pins

Motion (`kernel_laws`, `k6_pocket.rs`):
- `pocket_inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: the square pocket and the pocket with a round island; Auto, Inside and Outside (Waterline) cut the same multiset of rings (`Curve::same_cut`, 1 um, restart and reverse free).
- `pocket_rings_do_not_lift`: 0 lifts on the square pocket; each lift on the pocket with an island (Auto: 5, Outside: 4) has a named reason.
- `pocket_has_no_dead_end_ramp`: each ramp entry descends along its own first cut and ends at its start.
- `a_closed_pocket_without_a_safe_entry_is_refused_by_name`, `the_zigzag_pocket_is_refused_by_name_on_the_kernel`.
- `the_verifier_passes_each_kernel_pocket`, `pocket_2d_readings_of_the_kernel`.

Motion lib: `kernel_emit::tests::a_level_top_lets_the_approach_start_over_the_floor_above`, `kernel_region::tests::kernel_pocket_selection_drops_a_sliver_loop`.

App (`pocket_pass_start`, `kernel_route.rs`):
- `kernel_route_pocket_generates_verifies_and_posts`: a closed pocket through the real generate path with the engine `new`; no blocking verifier warning; it posts with the shipped Fanuc post.
- `kernel_route_default_engine_keeps_the_old_pocket`: the same op with the default engine is the old planner's path, move for move (the command, `generate_on(Old)` and `generate_on(default)`). The fig8 baseline goldens of #4153 (`kernel_baseline`) are unchanged.
- `kernel_route_refuses_what_the_recipe_does_not_plan`: Plunge in a closed pocket (`NO_SAFE_ENTRY`), Adaptive, rest machining; each other phase-1 kind is still refused under `new`.
- `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (heavy) and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`: fig8, Waterline, old against new with the law measures. Each start is planned or refused by name (Auto must plan); each lift of the kernel is named; the kernel lifts no more than the old planner; the verifier finds no unsafe kind, and `Crossing` (#4300) is the one blocking kind that the kernel adds.
- `offset_pass_start::planner_switch::switch_new_refuses_a_kind_it_does_not_plan_yet`: updated, the 2D Pocket now passes under `new`.

Kernel (`laws`): `registry::each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` runs L1-L7 and the link rule on the registered 2D Pocket.

The app suite includes the law measure helpers of `camcraft-motion` (`crates/motion/tests/common/law_measure`, `mask_grid`) with `#[path]`. They are test helpers that read a toolpath; no generator of another crate is imported.

## Gate results (final head)

All on head `42a68699e` (the final commit of this PR), Linux, `-j 6`:
- `cargo check --tests` for `camcraft-pathkernel`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` (one at a time): clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the same three crates: clean.
- Quick gate, `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (under `xvfb-run -a`): 463 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. It holds `pathkernel suites: laws`, `motion suites: kernel_laws`, `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, the motion pocket suites, `app suites: pocket_pass_start`, `offset_pass_start` and the other app pocket suites.
- Example catalog by name (in the quick plan, default switch): `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: ok.
- Light lane, `cargo xtask gate light`: 7 steps, 0 failed (`app light: pocket_pass_start` holds `fig8_pocket_kernel_baseline_light` and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`).
- The targeted heavy step of this P1 under the safety floor: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/side/path-kernel --only "app heavy: pocket_pass_start"`: ok (it holds `fig8_pocket_kernel_baseline`, the #4153 goldens of the default switch, unchanged, and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named`).

## Not exercised

- Zigzag, Adaptive, rest machining, "do not touch" and the corner relief on the kernel (refused by name, out of scope).
- A tilted (3+2) frame: the converter refuses a plane that is not the setup XY plane by name (`NOT_SETUP_XY`). No test generates a tilted 2D Pocket under `new`.
- Pre-drilled holes on the kernel route: the holes go into the entry choice, but no pin runs them.
- The example catalog under `new`: the catalog suites ran with the default switch only.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`. The main ones:
- The pass link `Retract` (the `Links::PLANAR` default) and `KeepDown` become "stay down where proved"; only `Clearance` is the user's retract between cuts.
- A lower level enters over the floor of the level above, where the approach of each entry stands on a cut of every level above (else from over the stock top). The first trial (each level from over the stock top) gave a helix through the cut levels and 6 more `Crossing` findings on fig8.
- The verifier gets the pocket area and the air round the stock (`kernel_pocket_reach`), so an air entry is no `Gouge` of the stock edge; the part walls stay judged.
- An incomplete verdict is refused; only a done verdict reaches the post.
- Zigzag waits for #3753.

Changelog: none (the default stays `old`, so no user sees a change; the switch-over PR writes the row).

Refs #3752

title: docs(process): the path kernel merges to main first, and the kinds switch one at a time
body:
## What changed

The delivery plan of the path kernel changed on 2026-11-27 (#4023, comment https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4023#issuecomment-7215353049). This PR makes the docs agree with it. It changes no code.

- New decision record `docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`. It quotes the maintainer's words of 2026-11-27, gives the new delivery (merge to `main` with the default at the old planner, a switch PR for each kind, removal after each switch, the four switch conditions for each kind, a question to the maintainer before the first switch), and names the sections of the K0 record (#4024 in `RECOMMENDED.md`) that it replaces. It lists what is dropped and what stays. `RECOMMENDED.md` is not edited.
- `AGENTS.md`, rule **Side branch** (the stable name stays):
  - the plan pointer: the file `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` does not exist; the rule now points to the `#4024` heading in `RECOMMENDED.md` and to the new record;
  - the bullet on the issue of a merged sub-PR: it keeps `in-review` until the switch PR of its kind, or until its own work is complete on `main`;
  - the last bullet: the PR from the side branch to `main` replaces the one switch-over PR.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: two lines that named the one switch-over PR (who merges a `side/*` PR, and the comment text on a sub-PR issue).
- The four lines of `AGENTS.md` that cite **Side branch** do not contradict the new text and are not changed. `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md` has no wrong line and is not changed.

## The new text of the rule

```text
- **Side branch** (#4023, #4042). A side branch `side/<name>` collects the
  sub-PRs of one large change. Then one PR takes it to `main`. Only the
  maintainer permits a side branch. `side/path-kernel` is the one that
  exists. It is made from `main` after this rule merges. Its plan is in
  `RECOMMENDED.md` under `## #4024 - Path kernel K0`, and its delivery is
  in `docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`.
  - The branch is protected against a force-push and a deletion. It is
    never rebased. Each change goes to it through a sub-PR.
  - A sub-PR has one issue. Its worktree is made from `origin/side/<name>`,
    on a branch `issue/N-<slug>`. It opens as a draft with `--base
    side/<name>`.
  - The body of a sub-PR starts with `Side branch: side/<name>`. It ends
    with `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`: a merge into a side branch closes no
    issue.
  - A sub-PR gets the quick pass and the collaborator review as each other
    PR. It merges with a merge commit when its review is clean, also as a
    `feat`. `--delete-branch` deletes only the sub-PR's own branch.
  - The issue of a merged sub-PR keeps `in-review` until the switch PR of
    its kind merges, or until the issue's own work is complete on `main`.
    The merging session comments `merged to side/<name> in PR #M; closes
    at the switch of its kind` on the issue.
  - `main` is merged into the side branch with `git merge`, through a sync
    PR into the side branch. Never rebase, never force-push. Do this after
    each merge batch on `main` that touches the code of the side branch,
    and at least each week. If the two sides changed the same logic, the
    sync stops and the maintainer decides (`resolve-conflicts` skill).
  - The gates are local: `post-merge.yml` covers `main` only. Each sub-PR
    runs its pinning tests, the quick gate of its diff against
    `origin/side/<name>`, the example catalog suites and the light lane.
    The head of the side branch gets one local batch gate after each sync,
    inside the build limit. A red batch is fixed on the side branch before
    the next sub-PR merges.
  - The lane and in-flight limits count a sub-PR as each other PR.
  - One PR takes `side/<name>` to `main`. It can come before the
    switches. It uses `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`. An issue closes with the
    switch PR of its kind or with its own work. The PR merges without
    `--delete-branch`. The maintainer's word for that PR says who merges
    it. For `side/path-kernel` it is the coordinator session (his answer
    of 2026-11-27). It merges when an independent review is clean on the
    head, and the batch gate, the heavy `motion` and `app` tests and the
    example catalog suites are green.
```

## Tests

Docs and process only. No build and no gate ran. `git grep` finds no other file that pins the changed strings (`switch-over`, `4024-path-kernel-design`) in `xtask/`, `crates/`, `scripts/` or `.claude/`.

Not exercised: no contract check reads these lines.

title: feat(tools): tool component bodies from STEP, STL and OBJ files
body:
## What changed

This PR is the mesh-body slice of #3643. A tool component body can now come from a STEP, STL or OBJ file. The body is placed by its own ISO 13399 mounting frame. All code is domain code in `camcraft-geometry` and `camcraft-tools`. There is no new crate edge, no app change and no UI change.

- `camcraft_geometry::step_csys`: `MCS_INSERT` is now `CsysRole::Mounting`. The app's `step_csys.rs` re-exports this type, so the app reads it too. A file that names both `MCS` and `MCS_INSERT` has two mounting frames, and `ToolCsysReport::find` refuses it as ambiguous.
- New `camcraft_tools::mesh_body::MeshBody`:
  - STEP: meshed by the existing kernel import (`camcraft_geometry::step::parse`) at a 0.01 mm chord, with its named coordinate systems.
  - STL (ASCII and binary) and OBJ: read by the new `camcraft_tools::mesh_file`, with frames that the caller stores (`with_frames`).
  - `parts()` reads the ports (CSW, CSWx, CSWx_y) and the CIP in the mounting frame (MCS or MCS_INSERT). A port or CIP that is not below the mounting frame is refused by name, because the MCS +Z must point toward the machine.
  - `spindle_geometry()` gives a `ComponentGeometry` with a `ComponentBody`: the revolved envelope of all facets, drawn as a stepped outline. The outline only grows the envelope, and a last check refuses a body whose outline does not enclose the envelope.
  - `lathe_geometry()` gives the ports, the CIP and a `LatheBody` for `resolve_lathe`. All bodies of the stack go to `LatheClearance::of` as one set, as #4194 does.
- Never smaller than the steel: a meshed STEP body grows by the certified chord deviation of the kernel. The spindle bands grow by it. The lathe clearance grows through the new `LatheBody::padded` and `LatheClearance::padded` (`lathe_clearance_pad.rs`).
- Facet budget: one component body has at most 1 000 000 facets. Past the budget, the body is refused by name, and the text names #1041. A STEP model is first meshed coarser by the existing importer.
- Corrupt or degenerate input gives a named refusal (`MeshBodyError`, `MeshFileError`), never a panic.
- `Frame::unmap_point`, `unmap_dir` and `relative` are new (the inverse of the frame map).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3643-mesh-bodies.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-geometry` `step_csys_read::mcs_insert_names_the_mounting_frame_and_two_mounts_are_ambiguous`
- `camcraft-tools` lib, `mesh_body_tests`:
  - `an_stl_holder_with_stored_frames_resolves_in_a_spindle_stack` (gauge length and band of a stack with an end mill)
  - `ascii_and_binary_stl_and_obj_read_the_same_facets`
  - `a_step_body_places_by_its_own_iso_13399_frames` (MCS and MCS_INSERT, deviation grow)
  - `lathe_bands_grow_by_the_pad`
  - `the_drawn_outline_never_falls_inside_the_envelope`
  - `a_missing_doubled_or_upside_down_frame_is_refused_by_name`
  - `degenerate_and_over_budget_files_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_corrupt_step_body_is_refused_by_name`
  - `mangled_files_never_panic` (a small fuzz pass over STL, OBJ and STEP)
- `camcraft-tools` lib, `lathe_assembly_tests::an_stl_holder_mesh_gives_the_box_holder_clearance` (the same clearance as the box holder, and the pad grow through `resolve_lathe`)

## Gate results (head d1eb8a1bcc8e37b31dca7b0679951a2a2659ef44)

- Windows (winbuild), log `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-3643d-d1eb8a1bcc8e37b31dca7b0679951a2a2659ef44.log`, first line `head d1eb8a1bcc8e37b31dca7b0679951a2a2659ef44`:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the diff touches `crates/geometry`, so quick falls back to batch. 1229 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (152.6 min).

title: fix(multiaxis): prove every swarf exit rise with an exact sweep
body:
## What changed

- New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp_sweep.rs`. It gives the exact distance from a tool axis that moves along a straight line (a parallelogram) to each facet. It uses the triangle-triangle distance law: vertex-to-triangle and edge-to-edge candidates, and an edge-crossing test.
- `stamp_rise::rapid_rise` uses this exact sweep. The old proof sampled the ball and the flank every r/2. The swept tool must now stay at least as far from the part as the start pose.
- The plan's own RAPID rises under a held lean now go through the same proof (`stamp_rise::rise_kind`). If the straight rise is not proved, the rapid moves out along the contact normal first, under the same pose (`normal_exit`). Then it rises, and then it crosses to the plan's top point. The exact sweep proves each leg. If no exit is proved, the rapid stays as the plan wrote it, and the verifier's rapid law judges it.
- `stamp.rs` posts the two via points of such an exit as rapids under the held pose. `stamp_link::contact_normal` is now `pub(super)`.

## Cause

The nine flagged moves are not the #48 feed rises. They are the plan's own retract rapids at the end of each side-pass level. The stamp gave each plan rapid the held lying pose, and nothing proved it. #4108 added the vertical-rapid sweep to the verifier, and this exposed them. The verifier is correct: each lift goes into the part by 0.013 to 0.24 mm.

A second gap was also real. The sampled proof did not see a facet edge between two samples. Move 2141 starts under the tube's equator. With only the rapid route fixed, the sampled proof still accepts move 2141.

title: fix(recognize): read a slot with holes through or tangent to its floor
body:
## What changed

`detect_pockets` returned no feature for the reported slot (p01-flange). This PR finds two causes and fixes both, in `crates/app/src/recognize`:

1. **A hole tangent to the slot wall.** The through holes at x 39..45 touch the slot wall at x 45. So the hole ring and the outer ring of the floor share one vertex. The feature walk (`geometry::feature::build_loops`) reports each ring through such a vertex as `Open`, so the floor had no outer ring and the reader skipped it. The new `recognize::pinch` takes the walk's split rings as the outer ring and its holes, but only when it can prove them:
   - each ring is simple, and each span of each ring is a boundary edge of the face;
   - each hole has a vertex off the outer ring, and those vertices are inside the largest ring;
   - the largest ring's area less the hole areas is the face's facet area (relative slack 1e-3).

   Any other knotted face stays refused, as before. The geometry walk does not change, so no `FaceId` moves.
2. **A hole through the slot floor.** `slot_of` refused each floor with an inner ring. Now it refuses a floor with a boss only: an inner ring with a facet above the floor on one of its edges (`walls::Mesh::rises_from`). A hole has its wall below the floor, so the floor still reads as a slot. `islands` still counts every inner ring.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/2440-slot-floor-holes.md`.

## Readings

The issue's part was rebuilt in SolidCraft (plate 100 x 60 x 10, slot x 35..45 with its floor at z 7, four 6 mm through holes at (±42, ±22)) and exported as STL. It was then read through `camcraft-cli mcp`.

- Before: `{"count": 0, "features": []}`.
- After: one `slot`, floor z 7, top z 10, `islands` 2, width 10, length 60, ends `["open", "open"]`, centreline x 40 from y 30 to y −30.
- `detect_pockets {create: 0}` makes `Slot1`. With the stock fitted to the part, `generate` is ok, `verify` has no finding, and `post` writes 34 lines.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_pockets.rs`)

- `a_slot_with_a_hole_tangent_to_its_wall_is_still_a_slot`: a hand-built, watertight block whose diamond hole touches the slot wall at one vertex. The test checks the slot, its ends, its width, its length and its floor area (400 − 18). It also checks that `create` makes a Slot that generates.
- `a_slot_with_holes_through_its_floor_is_still_a_slot`: a height field with two holes in the floor (no tangency).
- `a_boss_standing_in_the_channel_is_not_a_slot`: the same field with bosses. It is still an open pocket, as before.

The first two fail on `upstream/main` and pass with this change. The boss test passes on both, so it guards against a fix that counts every inner ring as a hole.

## Gates

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 5 steps, 0 failed (`app suites: mcp_pockets`, `app suites: pocket_recognition` and the build steps).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches 74 app heavy steps. They are not run yet. I will add the result in a comment before the PR is flagged ready.

## Not exercised

- A knotted face whose split fails the proof. It stays refused by code reading only; no test builds such a face.
- The UI Pockets page. It reads the same `recognize::pockets_of`, so it lists the same slots.

title: fix(ui): report failed window captures
body:
## What changed

A failed window read-back now answers the report request. The status says:

> Screenshot: picture was not copied - the text report is complete

The completion channel retains the tokens on map, mapped-range and decoding failures. The frame consumes failures before it draws the status strip. A failed picture never produces a screenshot event or a clipboard image. A foreign token does not change the report status.

The capture remains busy until the frame consumes its result. This keeps the final repaint after the callback clears its flag. Each shot owns its flag, so an obsolete callback after a timeout cannot release or answer a newer shot. Requests that arrived during a failed shot remain queued.

The change is limited to the native report capture, the frame call, five regression tests and the decision note. It adds no dependency or persistent fault-injection option.

## Reproduction and readings

On `a7afb5766b5d37073eb075ecda84c3ba70430653`, a cancelled read-back leaves the status at “is copying the window to the clipboard”. The new status assertion fails on that source. It passes with this change.

The test cancels a real pending wgpu map with `Buffer::unmap`. Linux uses the Vulkan llvmpipe software adapter. This exercises the production map-error callback. It does **not** simulate physical device loss. A separate deterministic test uses the shared callback completion helper and checks the visible status and absence of an image copy.

## Checks

On source head `e086568649de35370209c8067ca2fdb8834979a6`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: all 10 steps pass. This includes the UI library, the five new capture tests, the existing report tests and eight mapped UI suites.

- `cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: all 11 light twins pass in five steps.

The first unrestricted light command reached the foreground time limit during its broad release prebuild. No process remained. The precise command above compiled and ran every discovered light target successfully. The prebuild timeout is not reported as a passed step.

The regression tests cover:

- failed completion to visible status, without an image copy;
- cancellation through the real map callback;
- foreign tokens and a closed report dialog;
- successful delivery to multiple tokens and a queued request after failure;
- timeouts and late failure/success replies during a fresh shot.

No machining, G-code, post, geometry, collision or stock simulation behavior changes. No full heavy lane, GPU parity, example catalog or release package was run. A real lost device was not tested. No required CI rules were returned by the authenticated main rules and ruleset APIs; this is not a green-CI claim.

These are genuine Linux renders from a temporary test harness. It presses the real report button, cancels the native capture map, consumes the result and draws the production report/status components. ## What changed

1. **Auto reads the depth in material.** Auto chose the drill cycle by `R plane - bottom`, so the air above a hole's mouth counted as depth. A 3.5 mm spot under a 5 mm gap posted `G73 ...    - the setup sheet (`crates/app/src/setup_sheet/operations.rs`).

It gives the existing `CycleKind::Deep`, which every canned-cycle post writes as `G83`. It is appended at combo index 10 and digest byte 10, so older operations keep their indices and stamps. ## What changed

This PR adds four MCP post tools (`crates/app/src/mcp/post_tools.rs`):

- `list_posts` lists each built-in post and each `.cps` file in the user posts folder. Each row gives the machine kinds that the post serves, `description`, `program_units`, `extension` and the declared options. A file that does not load gives its `problem`. `selected` is the document's post.
- `select_post` runs `SelectPost` through the session History. It is one undo step. `null` selects the default built-in post.
- `preview_post` runs a script (`source` or `path`) on a built-in sample (Facing, Contour, Pocket, Drilling) or on the document stream. It writes no file. It returns `ok`, `program`, `lines`, `warnings` and `swallowed`. A failed script returns `ok: false` and `errors` with the 1-based `line` in the script. The Boa runtime limits stop a script that loops.
- `save_post_script` saves a plain file name in the user posts folder. The folder is `CAMCRAFT_POSTS`, else `<data dir>/camcraft/posts` (the same order as the user machines folder). The script must load and run before the save. An existing file is replaced only with `overwrite: true`. The write is atomic.

- In a live app session, `save_post_script` needs approval as a `FileWrite`, and `select_post` as a `LimitEdit` (`mcp::live::requires_approval`).

title: fix(sim): weight the B letter by |cos A| in the mid-pose swing bound
body:
Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4262#issuecomment-7209042252

## What changed

- `crates/sim/src/verify/midpose.rs`: the swing bound counts the B letter at `max |cos A|` over the move. A and C keep full weight. A new helper `max_abs_cos` gives the weight. A non-finite letter gives weight 1, which is the old bound.
- The module header states the new proof.
- One pinning test in `posed_steel_tests.rs` and one soundness test in `midpose.rs`.
- `docs/decisions/4262-housing-table-index.md`.

## Cause

The mid-pose walk bounds the axis turn in an interval from the letters' sweep. It counted each letter at one radian for each radian. The axis is `Rz(C) (cos A sin B, -sin A, cos A cos B)`, so B turns it only `|cos A|` for each radian.

`axis_to_angles` writes a radial pose under the A line as B180 and the same pose over it as B0. At A = -90 the pose crosses the equator with a B 180 -> 0 flip and no real turn. The old bound read that flip as a swing of about 90 degrees on one interval. The posed fixture sweep then grew the spindle housing capsule (300+ mm up the pose) by hundreds of mm. The grown capsule reached the machine table 510 mm below the axis. The post refused with "spindle housing at move N strikes a fixture".

This answers the question of the issue: the frames are correct. The refusal was phantom. It came from the swing bound, not from the frame math. The same bound inflated the part-frame fallback too.

## Tests

- Pin: `verify::posed_steel::tests::a_b_flip_at_the_pole_of_a_turning_a_does_not_swing_the_housing_into_the_table` (camcraft-sim lib). A tip 10 mm off the A line, the pose flips B180 -> B0 at A -90, the Doosan housing (r 75, 250 long), the Doosan table (top Z-510). It asserts Clear in the machine frame and no hit in the part frame, for +Y and -Y.
  - Red before the fix: `left: Hit(Spindle) right: Clear` ("machine frame, pose [0.0, 1.0, 1e-9]").
- Soundness: `verify::midpose::tests::the_cos_a_weighted_bound_holds_near_the_pole`. Four letter pairs near the pole, 64 samples in each interval: no pose inside an interval strays past its swing. A B flip at the pole gives a swing under 1e-8.
- Mutation 1: the old rate line back -> both tests red. Fix back -> both green.
- Mutation 2: `max_abs_cos` forced to 0 (an under-report) -> the soundness tests stay green. On the canonical letters the end-pose angles of each interval already bound the interior, so the letter-rate term rarely decides. The weight is proven from the derivative norms (decision file), not from this test.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head a5b1958eb: 135 steps, 0 failed. The base moved during the run, so the plan was wider than the diff. It includes `app suites: example_catalog` (44 passed, 4 ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy`: not run. This is a P3 PR. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a P3 PR no heavy step. The dry-run reach is 115 release steps. They run at the cut.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suite ran green and no `*.nc` or `*.cl` file changed. The change only makes a proven bound tighter, so a verdict can only go from hit to clear.

## Not exercised

- The reporter's project file. It is not in the issue. A model built from the issue text (R 9 x 30 cylinder on X, 30 x 44 x 44 box stock, 3 mm ball, Doosan + table, nose_to_axis stated) gave no fixture strike on main. It was refused for other reasons (uncut stock, a B word). So the end-to-end post of the report is not pinned. The pin reproduces the reported verdict at the sim law.
- The UI playback display (finding 1 of the contributor comment). It is display only and not part of this fix.
- The message does not name the struck box yet. That changes the `FixtureHit` warning and its readers. A follow-up issue will track it.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `verify/midpose.rs` or `verify/posed_steel*.rs`.

Effort: high

Changelog: The post no longer refuses a Rotary Flow on a turning A with a phantom "spindle housing strikes a fixture" when the radial pose crosses the A line's equator.

Fixes #4262

title: fix(app): generator defect fixes make cached toolpaths stale
body:
## The rule decided

Option 1, the lean rule the issue suggested, implemented at the salt: **a change of generator output that fixes a defect makes old caches stale.**

A named constant `GENERATOR_OUTPUT_VERSION` (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`) is written into every operation stamp. The PR that changes what a generator emits - a moved start, dive, lead, level or entry, any emitted move - bumps the number in the same PR. Every cache a project saved under the old number reads Stale once and clears on regenerate. A refactor whose output is byte-identical does not bump it. No auto-detection: the manual bump is the rule.

PR #3684 is exactly such a change, so a project saved before it now reads Stale instead of posting the old 18 mm plunge at the first tab window (#3453). The rule text sits in the stamp comment at the salt and in `docs/decisions/3704-generator-output-version.md`.

Dropped: option 2 (the wrong path would post silently, which the Prime Directive refuses); auto-detecting output changes (heavy, can miss); a per-kind version (every future fix would re-decide the scope; one number is the lean rule).

## The one-time churn

The term moves every stamp once, the same churn the v3/v4 salt bumps produced. It moves more than the saved stamps: the refreshed caches also hold regenerated moves, regenerated parameters and the current project-file version. So the committed project goldens were refreshed, catalog cases with `cargo xtask catalog`, the guide examples with their suites' `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` runs. Every `.nc` golden is byte-identical: the generator output of the current tree does not change.

## Goldens moved

Every changed project under `examples/` (the 15 catalog cases plus the 3 guide examples). Each row: stamp + cache refresh by the version bump; `.nc` byte-identical in all rows.

- `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket/adaptive-pocket.camproj` - stamp and cache refresh; pocket cached moves regenerated
- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.camproj` - stamp and cache refresh

This PR closes the three open items that #4271 listed for the tool library window (U7).

The bores come from the ER table that the holder library already has (`holder_library::ER_SIZES`, ISO 15488 series, DIN 6499 collet ranges). There is one collet for each whole millimetre. title: feat(motion): the converter from a kernel plan to a toolpath
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

## What changed

This PR adds the converter from a kernel `Plan` to a `Toolpath` in `camcraft-motion` (`crates/motion/src/kernel_emit/`). No old planner and no app code calls it. With the default planner switch, the output does not change. The first recipe (#3752) calls it.

The converter emits the steps of each level in the plan's order. It makes no decision of its own. It refuses a step that it cannot emit, with a named reason. It never drops a step and it never adds a cut.

Public surface (`camcraft_motion::kernel_emit`):
- `emit_plan(&Plan, WorkPlane, EmitHeights, EmitFeeds) -> Result<Emitted, EmitRefusal>`
- `emit_levels(&[LevelPlan { plan, plane }], EmitHeights, EmitFeeds) -> Result<Emitted, EmitRefusal>` (the levels in the order that the caller gives)
- `EmitHeights::new(clearance_z, top_z)` and `EmitFeeds::new(cut, plunge)`: checked values
- `Emitted { path, cut_moves: Vec<Range<usize>>, entries, stays, lifts, exits }`
- `EmitRefusal { reason(), level(), step() }`, `Display` and `Error`
- The refusal constants: `BAD_HEIGHTS`, `BAD_FEEDS`, `NOT_SETUP_XY`, `AXIS_NOT_NORMAL`, `UNKNOWN_STEP`, `ENTRY_NOT_CLEAR`, `APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`, `STEP_OFF_TOOL`, `STEP_NOT_DOWN`, `ENDS_DOWN`, `ARC_OFF_CIRCLE`, `ARC_NOT_MONOTONE`, `CUT_DROPPED`, `NOT_FINITE`

The move rules (the safety floor):
- A lateral rapid is only at or above the clearance height. A rapid along the tool axis goes only up: the retract of a lift or of an exit.
- The move down from the clearance height to the approach is a plunge-feed move.
- Below the stock top there are only the moves of a proved step: a cut, a stay-down link, the descent and lead of an entry, the lead-out of an exit.
- Each step must start where the tool stands. Else the converter refuses with `STEP_OFF_TOOL`.
- A lift is a retract to the clearance height. Its named reason goes to the notes in the text form of `links.rs` (`link: the tool lifted to the clearance height N time(s) instead of the keep-down in-plane link - <reason>; ...`).
- A cut whose curve holds an exact circle becomes G2/G3 arcs (quarter turns that end on plan points). Arc leads, helices and ramps are chords in the plan (#4178 point 5). The converter emits them as feeds.
- The converter refuses a plane that is not the setup XY plane (`NOT_SETUP_XY`). The mapping reads the `WorkPlane`: Z is the plane origin plus the depth.

No kernel source changes. No accessor was added to the kernel crate.

The merge of `side/path-kernel` (df9ec30, the load stage of #4265) gave a conflict in the K4 test helper. The resolution keeps both sides: the load stage goes between order and link in the plan builder, and the path goes through the real converter.

The merge-time refresh merges `side/path-kernel` (fd653b0, PR #4275: the approach from the air of #4254). Two files conflicted:
- `k3_load.rs`: the Outside rows of #4275 hold on the merged tree with the cuts-only path of this PR. The row 337 / 77 of this PR is replaced.
- `k4_order_link.rs`: the module text of both sides is kept. The pin keeps the real converter and takes the lift counts of #4275 (0 on each case).

The converter emits the approach stretches as feeds of a stay-down link. It refuses nothing.

## Pins

- `kernel_emit::tests` (motion lib, 7 tests):
  - `each_step_kind_gives_its_moves`
  - `a_lift_writes_its_reason_to_the_notes`
  - `an_exact_circle_becomes_arcs`
  - `levels_are_emitted_in_the_given_order`
  - `nothing_is_dropped` (the count of cuts in equals the count of cut move groups out)
  - `a_step_that_cannot_be_emitted_is_refused_by_name`
  - `an_empty_plan_gives_an_empty_path`
- `kernel_laws::k4_order_link::kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`: the test helper is replaced. The test now builds the whole plan (guide, order, link, entry and exit stage, with a helix asked) and converts it with the real converter. The helper asserts the converter's counts of cuts, entries, stay-down links, lifts and exits against the plan. On the merged tree:
  - 0 lifts on each case (#4275)
  - each lift named
  - the feed crossings as measured (`CROSSINGS`): disc Outside 3, dog bone Outside 1, Inside 0 (see the findings, follow-up #4300)
- `kernel_laws::k6a_plan_emit::the_verifier_finds_no_rapid_into_stock_and_no_plunge_without_an_entry` (new): the `camcraft-sim` verifier on the converted disc and dog-bone plans, Inside and Outside. It finds no `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock` and no `Gouge`. Each descent below the stock top is a plan entry. Each descent into solid stock is a helix or a ramp.

## Readings and findings

| Fixture | Moves | Lifts (named) | Entries | Verifier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| disc, Inside | 7336 | 0 | 1 into solid (read as a ramp: the helix is chords) | nothing |
| disc, Outside | 6497 | 0 | 1 in air | 3 `Crossing` |
| dog bone, Inside | 5368 | 0 | 1 into solid (ramp) | nothing |
| dog bone, Outside | 4719 | 0 | 1 in air | 1 `Crossing` |

These readings are on the merged tree (with #4275). Before #4275: 7355, 6402 (13 lifts, 14 entries), 5368, 4784 (15 lifts, 16 entries), and no verifier warning.

- **New with the merge: feed crossings in the air (Outside).** A stay-down link of #4275 runs along the air line (y -29) to the door of its approach. It crosses the arc lead of the first entry (moves 2 to 11). Disc: moves 189, 1664 and 1882 cross move 5 at (-38.398, -28.993). Dog bone: move 33 crosses move 5 at (4.587, -28.866). The link stage proves a link against the cuts, the links and the planned cuts, not against the leads of the entry stage. The kernel's test pen emits no leads, so #4275 read 0. The verifier finds no `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock` and no `Gouge`: it reports the crossings as `Crossing` warnings only. The K4 pin asserts the counts as measured, so a new crossing makes it red. Follow-up: #4300 (the link proof reads the entry leads).
- The disc Inside path has 7336 moves, not 7355: the link tries of #4275 change some link routes. No count changes.

- First, the verifier area was the band of `fixture::band` (the stock grown by 2 tool radii, less the part). With that area, the verifier gave 72 and 84 `Gouge` warnings on Outside. Each one is on an air entry or its arc lead outside the band, 17 mm or more from the part. The pin now uses the stock grown by 4 tool radii, less the part. No warning is near the part.
- The law measure reads Outside feeds outside `fixture::centre_reach`: 44 (disc) and 52 (dog bone) before #4275, 4 and 3 on the merged tree (one air entry each). These are the arc leads in the air. This is a reading of the entry stage, not of the converter. No pin asserts it.
- **The side head df9ec30 was red in `k3_load`.** #4265 was gated on a branch without #4253 (the link edge band). title: fix(ui): draw the machine's rotary kinematics in sim playback
body:
fix(ui): draw the machine's rotary kinematics in sim playback

## What changed

The sim playback drew a posed rotary tool about its own tip while the
work stayed at its document pose - the opposite of what a work-turning
rotary does. Now the playback reads the machine's kinematics:

- The timeline carries each op's rotary axis line. `sim::Seg` and
  `sim::Frame` grow a `work: Option<WorkTurn>` field (origin + dir,
  display only, `None` by default - no law reads it, so no verdict
  moves). The script builder (`shell::sim_script`) fills it per op with
  the very line the gate's posed-steel laws judge
  (`fixture::rotary_axis_of`): the stated op/machine line through the
  WCS origin, else the free fit - and only on a mounted machine whose
  chain states a work-turning rotary (`turns_part`, the machine
  editor's flag).
- Work-turning rotary (table A, the reporter's case): the draw stands
  the frame's pose upright about the line - the same signed turn
  `verify::posed_steel::upright_turn` computes - and carries the tip
  with it. The tool (cutter, shank, holder, housing) draws upright at
  the carried tip station; the part, the stock and the steel ride the
  turn. The math lives in the new `camcraft_app::sim_machine_view`
  (a mirror of the gate's Rodrigues turn, with its own unit tests).
- Tool-turning head: the machine file states no gauge-line pivot for a
  head, so the playback keeps today's tip-relative draw rather than
  guess a pivot. Noted here as the simplification the issue allows; a
  follow-up can draw head stations once the machine grammar states a
  pivot for them.
- Mill-turn (both present): the work-turning rotary drives the scene
  turn; a pose that cannot stand upright under the line (a head's tilt
  mid-travel, a leaning line) falls back to the tip-relative draw for
  that frame. Display is best-effort; nothing is refused.

The turn angle per frame is read off `Frame::axis` (a few flops); the
line is the knowledge the timeline carries, so the renderer never
re-derives machine data per frame.

## Fallback

No machine, no `turns_part` rotary, a non-rotary kind, a degenerate
line, or an unstandable pose: exactly today's draw, bit for bit.

## Screenshots

The microARC 4 bar job (Rotary Parallel on the 770MX + microARC 4) at
an indexed pose, captured off-screen with the guide-images Harness
pattern (PNGs on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch only):

Before - the whole assembly swung about the tip, driving the 250 mm
housing down through the table:
https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-4266/sim-playback-before.png

After - the work turned about the A line, the spindle upright at the
carried tip station:
https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-4266/sim-playback-after.png

## Tests

- `camcraft_app::sim_machine_view` unit tests: the turn stands a
  tipped pose vertical (the gate's sign), points on the line stay,
  radii hold, the tool stands upright at its carried station, and the
  fallback (a vertical C line, a pose along the line, a degenerate
  direction) draws what the playback drew before.
- `camcraft-sim`: `Frame` carries `work` through `Script::at` (all
  5 windows), default `None`.

Display only: no gate, generation or posted-output change.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` - green (280 lib + suites)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` - green (325)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - green (1717)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui
  --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean

Changelog: the sim playback now draws a work-turning rotary's real
kinematics - the work turned about the stated rotary axis line, the
tool upright - instead of a tool swung about its own tip.

title: feat(pathkernel): an Outside piece starts at the stock edge with a proved approach from the air
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4254#issuecomment-7207515978 (worker K4c-air-approach).

## What changed

A stay-down link can now end with an approach from the air. The approach is a straight stretch from the nearest place of the air to the start of an open piece on a stock edge loop. The link stage proves it. The plan has no new step kind, and the transition table of `Plan::new` does not change.

- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/approach.rs` (new): the approach proof and the fourth try of the link (`from_air`).
- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/proof.rs`: the chord proof is split into its room test, its crossing test and its swath test. The three tries of K4 are now one function (`tries`), so that the way out to the air uses them.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/route.rs`: `project` is visible to the link module.
- The order stage does not change (decision 4 in the record).

## The rule

The next cut must be an open piece whose start is on a stock edge loop. The approach starts at the place of an air loop nearest to that start, within a tool radius. The approach holds only when all of these are true:

- Each sample is in the air or the edge band, out of the part zone, more than a tool radius from each keep-out area, and not inside the cutter-centre area.
- The stretch holds in the legal room of the entry stage.
- The stretch crosses no cut made and no link, and touches no planned cut away from the ends of the link.
- The disc swept along the stretch, less the swath of the next piece, lies within a tool radius of the air. The air starts one tool radius outside the stock, so that rest is outside the stock.

Thus each piece of stock that the approach cuts is also cut by the next piece. The test is exact polygon geometry. Its only tolerance is the polygon flattening (`AREA_TOL`, 2 x `ROOM_TOL` = 10 um). No strip of uncut stock is open by a constant.

A piece whose start is not on a stock edge keeps the present rule. Where no proof holds, the link lifts with the reason of the straight link.

## Pins

Negative pins first (`crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/air_approach.rs`, in the `laws` directory suite):

- `an_approach_that_would_cut_stock_off_the_curve_is_refused`: a tooth of stock beside the start. A mutation run without the area test makes this pin fail.
- `an_approach_near_a_keep_out_at_the_stock_edge_is_refused`
- `an_approach_beside_a_part_that_reaches_out_of_the_stock_is_refused`
- `a_piece_that_does_not_start_at_the_stock_edge_keeps_its_lift_and_its_reason`

Positive pins:

- `a_link_comes_in_from_the_air_to_a_piece_at_the_stock_edge`
- `each_approach_of_the_bands_cuts_only_the_swath_of_its_piece`: each approach of the disc band and the dog-bone band is checked against the stock box of the case, not against the kernel's air.

Pins measured again, with no constant tuned:

- `order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named`
- `k4_order_link::kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (it now also prints the places of the full-width feeds)
- `k3_load::kernel_load_control_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (merged in PR #4265; it reads the same Outside plans)
- `link_rule::a_link_leaves_a_cut_at_the_stock_edge_runs_in_the_air_and_comes_back_over_cleared_stock`: its first assertion pinned the old refusal. That link now stays as an approach.

## Readings

| Fixture (Auto / Inside / Outside) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| disc pocket (law suite) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| disc band (law suite) | 13 / 0 / 13 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| dog-bone band (law suite) | 15 / 0 / 15 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| pocket with an island (law suite) | 7 / 7 / 5 | 7 / 7 / 5 |

| Motion pin | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| disc, Inside | 0 lifts, 0 crossings | 0 lifts, 0 crossings |
| disc, Outside | 13 lifts, 0 crossings; over 402, worst 145, full 0 | 0 lifts, 0 crossings; over 415, worst 145, full 0 |
| dog bone, Inside | 0 lifts, 0 crossings | 0 lifts, 0 crossings |
| dog bone, Outside | 15 lifts, 0 crossings; over 724, worst 167, full 0 | 0 lifts, 0 crossings; over 739, worst 180, full 1 |

The record's target of 0 lifts on the disc is met. No lift stays on the disc.

On the dog bone one approach arrives at full width, at (-2.40, 25.00) on the top stock edge. The material is in the swath of the next piece. Thus it is not a gouge and not stock off the curve. But no stage reads that load yet, because the load stage reads the cuts and not the links. Follow-up: #4272.

The K3 rows (moves above the limit, worst degrees, unnamed moves) change on Outside only. Disc: none 402/145/13 to 415/145/19; constant 334/118/74 to 344/122/81. Dog bone: none 724/167/3 to 739/180/13; constant 678/143/66 to 683/143/69. The decision record has the table.

This PR adds eight MCP tools for tool components, tool assemblies and the user component library. The tools are in three new files of `crates/app/src/mcp/`: `component_tools.rs`, `assembly_tools.rs` and `component_library_tools.rs`.

- `get_tool_assembly`: gives the component stack of a document tool. It gives each node with its mount (parent, port, Z rotation, stickout `projection_mm`), its MCS frame and its sync status. Document write tools. Each tool runs the same undoable command as the GUI, in one History step:
- `upsert_tool_component` (`UpsertDocumentComponent`)
- `delete_tool_component` (`DeleteDocumentComponent`)
- `set_tool_assembly` (`SetToolAssembly`; `links: null` clears the stack)

User library tools. These are file edits through `component_library::store`, not undoable commands:

title: fix(sim): the field simulator cuts a move past the per-move ceiling in pieces, so Stock cuts what the column engine cuts
body:
## What changed

`SdfField::subtract_batch` refuses a chord whose swept window adds more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` cells beyond the tool at rest. No caller segmented, so through `Stock` the field engine refused ordinary moves that the column engine cuts.

- `SdfField::subtract_batch_fitted` (new, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_cut.rs`) is `subtract_batch` with each chord or arc piece whose travel exceeds the ceiling cut as the fewest equal pieces that each fall under it. It finds the count by doubling until the pieces fall under it, then by bisection below that count. A chord splits at equal fractions of its ends. An arc piece splits into equal angular parts on the same circle, with Z shared out evenly (`ArcPiece::split`, `field_arc.rs`). Pieces shorter than one cell shrink no window further, so past that count it refuses by name. A sweep that is neither a chord nor an arc piece cannot be split and refuses by name.
- The six field arms of `Stock` cut through it, one call each: `simulate_field_with` (`backend.rs`), `simulate_undercut` (`field_undercut.rs`), the lathe arm (`field_lathe.rs`), the display arm (`display.rs`), and the single-move `subtract_flat` and `cut_chord` (`backend_edit.rs`).
- `subtract_batch` and `subtract` keep the refusal as the bound of one update. The pin `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` now checks that refusal on `subtract_batch` directly, and checks that `subtract_batch_fitted` cuts the same chord. Its block is now `SdfField::from_box` and it cuts the chord once (5.9 s in debug, from 259 s with three mesh-built fields and two cuts).

Where this differs from the issue: the issue proposed splitting `Move`s in each caller. This PR splits inside the field, at the chord and arc piece, because those are the units the ceiling measures. A move carries an arc, a pose and a C angle, and each caller would need its own interpolation of them. One split there covers every arm. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/4179-segment-to-ceiling.md`.

## Pinning tests

Synthetic blocks only, cell 0.254 mm, all in `crates/sim/tests/field_wide_tool.rs`. For the old code, `subtract_batch_fitted` was made to refuse as `subtract_batch` does, which is main's behaviour through `Stock`:

| Test | Old behaviour | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `an_endmills_300_mm_pass_cuts_on_both_engines` (the issue's steps) | fails: the field engine refuses | passes |
| `a_127_mm_tools_6_mm_plunge_cuts_on_both_engines` | fails: refused | passes |
| `an_undercut_discs_6_mm_plunge_cuts_through_simulate_undercut` | fails: refused | passes |
| `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` | fails at the fitted chord | passes |
| `the_single_move_stock_arms_cut_the_long_chord` (`subtract_flat`, `cut_chord`) | fails: `subtract_flat` refuses ("segment it") | passes |
| `a_127_mm_tools_helical_entry_cuts_on_both_engines` (arc split) | fails: refused (release) | passes (release, 328 s) |
| `a_wide_tools_short_move_cuts_on_the_field_engine_as_on_the_column_engine` (unchanged) | passes | passes |

The helical test is `#[ignore]`: it takes about 22 min in debug, past the 60 s rule in `AGENTS.md`. `camcraft-sim` is not in xtask's `HEAVY_CRATES` (`kernel`, `motion`, `app`), so no gate runs it. It was run by hand with `cargo test --release -p camcraft-sim --test field_wide_tool -- --ignored a_127_mm_tools_helical_entry_cuts_on_both_engines`.

## Gates

On head `6954260e9` (gates run against upstream/main `903e420b3`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 85 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (12.7 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Trial merge with upstream/main `903e420b3`: clean (`git merge-tree`).

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes. The helical test runs in no gate; it was run by hand only (above).
- A tilted tool past the ceiling. It rides the chord path, the same split as the straight pass, but no pin uses a tilt.
- The lathe arm past the ceiling: it calls the same method, but no pin turns past it.
- In our own lane (outside this repository), three programs with a 127.4 mm slitting disc plunging 15 to 28 mm were refused before this change. Those programs are not attached; the pins above are the evidence here.

title: feat(tools)!: .camtools version 8 carries tool components and stacks
body:
Stacked on #4233. This PR contains the commits of #4233. Merge #4233 first; then this PR takes `git merge origin/main` and a new gate. Do not merge this PR before #4233.

## What changed

This is slice 2 of #3645: the `.camtools` export and import of tool components and tool stacks.

- `.camtools` version 8 (`ASSEMBLY_VERSION`):
  - A definition of an assembled tool holds its stack as `assembly`. These are the `project::assembly_wire` links, as a `.camproj` tool states them.
  - The file holds a top-level `components` array with the rows that the exported stacks name. The rows use the wire form of `project::component_wire` from #4233.
  - The version step is conditional. A library without a stack keeps its older number (1 to 7) and the same bytes.
- Strict reading (`crates/app/src/tool_library/assembly.rs`):
  - The table is read whole. Each row is built again and refused by its id.
  - Each stack must name rows of the table and resolve, or the file is refused by the tool name.
  - A row that no stack names is refused by its id.
  - A file of version 7 or older that states `components` or `assembly` is refused.
  - The body of an assembled tool goes through `as_derived`, as on a project open (new `project::stack_from_dto`).
- Import (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/`):
  - `ImportTools` lands the rows and the tools in its one undo step. The table changes first on apply and is restored last on undo.
  - The rows land in the order of the file table, so an export after the import gives the same bytes.
  - An added or renamed tool gets its stack. An updated or replaced tool takes the library stack. A library tool without a stack clears the old stack on update, because the record does not come from that stack any more.
  - "Holders off" leaves out the stacks and their rows with the bodies.
  - `ImportReport` names the added and the reused rows.
  - The number laws moved to `tool_import/numbers.rs` without a change, to keep `mod.rs` below 400 lines.
- The id rule (`docs/decisions/3645-camtools-v8.md`). A library row whose id the document already holds:
  - same content (name, item, geometry): the document row is reused;
  - different content: the import is refused by the id, and nothing lands.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/camtools_v8.rs` (a new submodule of the existing `tool_library_holders` suite; no new top-level binary):

- `an_export_of_assembled_tools_is_version_8_and_imports_identically`
- `a_library_of_plain_tools_keeps_its_older_number_and_imports_as_before`
- `a_newer_version_and_an_older_file_with_components_are_refused`
- `a_bad_row_a_bad_link_or_an_unused_row_refuses_the_file_by_name`
- `undo_and_redo_of_an_import_with_components_restore_tools_and_table`
- `a_document_row_of_the_same_id_is_reused_when_the_same_and_refuses_when_different`

## Gate results (head `26eab082f`)

The base of the quick gate is the head of #4233 (`745234df7`). All runs are local, on the Mac.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base 745234df7`), at `323e1430a`: 200 steps, 198 ok, 2 red. The red steps were `holder_reference` and `tool_library`. Their tests named version 8 as the first unknown number. The fix moves them to version 9.
- The red steps again (`--failed`) on the fix: 2 ok.
- On the final head `26eab082f` (the only later change is a `type` alias for clippy and the test fix): `app suites: tool_library_holders`, `tool_library`, `holder_reference`, `tool_import_modes`, `tool_table`: all ok. The pinning tests (`gate test camtools_v8`): 6 ok.
- Strict clippy (`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`) on the final head: clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`) on the final head: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Example catalog suites: not needed. No post and no toolpath changed. They are in the quick plan and were ok.

## Not exercised

- The MCP reply and the UI import page do not show the component counts yet. The MCP tools are #3647 and the UI is #3648.
- A stack in the bare `[{name, definition}]` array is refused, because that form has no table.

Changelog: `.camtools` tool libraries now carry tool components and tool assemblies (version 8). The import adds the components in the same undo step, reuses a component of the same content, and refuses a different component of the same id.

Effort: high (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a `.camtools` file with assembled tools is version 8. Builds that read version 7 and older refuse it.

What remains on #3645: nothing of the issue text after this PR. This PR merges after #4233, so it closes the issue. The MCP tools (#3647) and the UI (#3648) are separate issues.

Fixes #3645

title: feat(app): multi-seat indexable cutters take their whole record from the document
body:
## What changed

This PR is the app part of #3646. It builds on the #4201 component commands. It does not depend on PR #4233, and it does not touch `crates/app/src/project/`.

- `DocumentComponent` (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`) has two new fields:
  - `milling: Option<MillingBody>`: the catalog facts of a multi-seat cutter body. Only a tool item can have them.
  - `running: Option<InsertRunning>`: the tool material and the cutting rows of an insert. Only an insert can have them.
- `tool_assembly::derive`: when the insert sits on a body row with cutter facts, the tool gets the whole milling record from the #4192 resolver (`milling_cutter::derive(..).assembled(..)`). This includes the kind, the diameter, the corner, the flutes, the flute length, centre cutting and the enclosed holder. The resolver checks every seat. The running data of the insert goes on each tool that cuts with that insert. This includes the single-seat insert path.
- `UpsertDocumentComponent::with_row` and `EditDocumentComponent::with_row` take the whole row. `EditDocumentComponent::new` keeps the facts and the running data of the held row. The command refuses a fact on the wrong kind of component when the row is made. It also refuses running rows that a milling tool cannot take.
- An edit of the shared insert updates each tool that uses it in one undo step. The operations go Stale through their stamps, as in #3644.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3646-multi-seat-record.md`.

## Pinning tests

New submodule `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/multi_seat.rs`, in the existing `tool_library_holders` binary (no new top-level binary):
- `a_multi_seat_cutter_takes_its_whole_record_from_the_document`: a 4-seat Ø50 face mill and a 2-seat Ø25 end mill with one shared insert. Each tool gets the flutes, the flute length, centre cutting, the tool material and the cutting rows.
- `a_shared_insert_edit_updates_both_multi_seat_tools_in_one_undo_step`: the corner and the cutting rows change on the two tools, the two operations go Stale, and undo and redo restore the exact state.
- `an_edit_that_breaks_a_seat_is_refused_by_the_tool_name`: a D insert in the S seats, and `DC` away from the seats, are refused. The refusal names the component and the tool, and nothing changes.
- `the_face_mill_is_refused_a_plunge_into_solid`: the face mill (not centre-cutting) gets `CENTER_CUT_REFUSAL` on a tight Bore. The centre-cutting end mill bores its hole.

body:
The parent #4242 is merged (`82afe9d8f`); this PR now shows only its own commits.

## What changed

This is the first slice of #4095. The issue stays open for the rest.

- New: one HEIDENHAIN dialect resolver in the post crate, `camcraft_post::post::heidenhain_dialect` (table in `heidenhain_profiles.rs`). It maps `controller.identity` (model, NC software, installed options) to a profile and a flag set. The post engine gives the result to each script as `machine.heidenhainDialect`: the flags, or `{ "error": "<why>" }`.
- The resolver parses the canonical values of `docs/research/heidenhain/dialects.md` section 1. It refuses by name an unknown model, a paraxial model (TNC 124/128), a malformed NC software identifier, release `00`, an unnamed release, a variant outside its family, and a malformed option number.
- DIN/ISO post (`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`):
  - The resolver replaces the #4172 table (`drillLevel()` now reads `drillC200`).
  - A stated control that the resolver refuses, or that has no DIN/ISO programs (`languageIso`), is refused by name at the program start.
  - `G247 Q339=n` is refused by name where cycle 247 is not a preset-table row (`cycle247`).
  - A machine with no controller identity keeps the output of today.
- Klartext post (`assets/posts/heidenhain-klartext.cps`):
  - The resolver replaces the fixed language check. A profile that does not confirm M140, cycle 247 as a preset-table row and M137 is refused by name. Coordinates use the profile's `decimals`.
  - The manual quill procedure stays verified for iTNC 530 NC 340490-03 only (#4114). The refusal now names the resolved profile.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/4095-heidenhain-dialect-resolver.md`. It lists each flag with its research source.

## Flags wired, with sources

| Flag | Post use | Source (`docs/research/heidenhain/differences.md`) |
|---|---|---|
| `languageIso` | DIN/ISO: refuse when not `yes` | B2 "DIN/ISO programs" |
| `decimals` | Klartext: coordinate rounding; DIN/ISO: writes 3, refuses fewer | B2 "Coordinate decimals" |
| `drillC200` | DIN/ISO: G200 with or without Q395; `base` refused | B2 "Cycle 200 Q list", B3 |
| `cycle247` | DIN/ISO: G247 only for `presetTable`; Klartext: refuse otherwise | B2 "Cycle 247 DATUM SETTING" |
| `m140`, `m136m137` | Klartext: refuse when not `yes` | B2 "M140"; section B (iTNC 530 340 420, TNC 410) |
| `dwell` | no branch: DIN/ISO always writes `G04 F` (#4093); pinned on a `functionDwell` control | B2 "Cycle 9", "FUNCTION DWELL" |
| `toolCallByName`, `toolNameMax` | resolved and table-tested; no branch, both posts write the tool number form | B2 "Tool name in quotes", "Name length" |

## Golden output

- No golden file changes. The Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03) resolves to `itnc-49x`, which gives the output of today for both posts.
- Behaviour changes only for identities that no shipped machine file states. The decision file lists them (for example TNC 320 340 551-01 to -03 are now refused by the DIN/ISO post, and iTNC 530 340 420 now posts G200 at the Q211 level).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib, `post::heidenhain_dialect::tests` (13 tests): each version boundary of each wired flag on both sides, the Picomax profile, refusals of unknown and paraxial models, malformed identifiers, unnamed releases, option numbers, the script value.

- `heidenhain_cycles::presets`: `a_preset_table_control_selects_the_row`, `g247_is_refused_where_cycle_247_is_not_a_preset_row`.
- `heidenhain_block_form`: the dwell test now pins `G04 F` on TNC 426 280 472 and TNC 410 (3 decimals), and a refusal of a spaced NC string.
- `script_heidenhain_klartext::dialect_tests`: `the_dialect_resolver_decides_the_klartext_profile`, `the_picomax_profile_writes_four_decimals`.

title: feat(wire): control and wear wire offset for Wire Contour (COMP records for the LN2W post)
body:
Process change: yes

## What changed

- A Wire Contour has a new parameter, `compensation`: `computer` (the default, as before), `control` or `wear`.
- The generator makes and judges the same wire-centre path as before. With `control` or `wear`, each pass then gets one `CompSpan` (`motion::wire_edm::wire_comp_spans`, a new module `comp.rs`).
  - Control: the span's programmed geometry is the part contour. Each ring move moves back by the offset along its normal. A line moves by translation, an arc keeps its centre and changes its radius. Two lines at a mitred joint meet at the part corner. A corner round that the offset put in collapses to its corner.
  - Wear: the programmed geometry is the wire-centre walk itself.
  - Each span states its pass's kerf offset (wire radius plus the gap of the pass's condition) as its radius. The rough pass is first, then each skim.
- The post dump already writes a span between `COMP` records (M13.11). So the LN2W post of #4139 writes `G41` / `G42 Hnnn` by pass, with `C001` and `H001` first, and `G40` on each lead-out. The post and the engine do not change.
- The command door (`wire_gate`) and the generator refuse control or wear by name with: an open run, a 4-axis cut, a taper, a burnout, tabs, the arc lead, an exit pick (`operation::wire_comp::refusal`).
- The span builder refuses by name: a lead-in or lead-out shorter than the pass's offset, an arc lead, a pass that does not return to the start hole, a hairpin turn, an arc at a sharp joint.
- Mark 21, G-EDM and the other wire posts refuse the offset by name (their existing hooks, or the engine's refusal).
- Project file: the key `compensation` is written only when it is not `computer`. The stamp digests it only then. No existing file or stamp changes.
- MCP: the parameter rides the operation DTO, so `add_operation` and `edit_operation` take it. `list_operation_types` lists it. The `camcraft-mcp` skill row names it (a process file: `Process change: yes`).
- Each `WireContourOp` literal in the tests gets `compensation: Default::default()`.

## Cause

`posting_wire.rs` posted only the wire-centre path, and the op had no mode. No LN2W program with the control's offset could come from the app (#4134).

## Item 3 of the issue: how the wire laws judge the path

The kerf, threading and slug laws judge the wire-centre moves, as before. These moves are what the control cuts when each register holds the radius that its span states. The post writes that radius in the comment before each `G41` / `G42` line (`THE STREAM STATES 0.165 MM`). The decision is in `docs/decisions/4134-wire-control-offset.md`.

## Tests

Pins (all new):

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::comp::tests` (9): `a_die_square_is_programmed_on_its_profile_under_g41`, `a_punch_square_is_programmed_on_its_profile_under_g42`, `a_reversed_skim_takes_the_other_side`, `each_pass_states_its_own_radius`, `the_wear_span_programs_the_wire_centre_moves`, `computer_compensation_records_nothing`, `a_circle_is_programmed_as_arcs_at_the_part_radius`, `a_lead_in_shorter_than_the_offset_is_refused_by_name`, `an_arc_lead_and_an_open_run_are_refused_by_name`.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_post`, `sodick_aq600l::offset` (5): `the_ln2w_square_posts_the_part_contour_with_the_controls_offset`, `the_ln2w_two_axis_block_posts_the_part_arcs_with_the_controls_offset`, `the_ln2w_square_posts_the_wire_centre_path_with_a_wear_offset`, `the_mark_21_post_refuses_the_controls_offset_by_name`, `the_offset_with_a_taper_or_an_open_run_is_refused_at_the_door`.
- `camcraft-app` lib, `the_wire_compensation_round_trips_and_is_absent_for_computer`.
- `mcp_wire_contour::list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law` now includes `compensation`.

Red before the fix: the pins do not compile on `upstream/main` (no `compensation` field, no `wire_comp_spans`).

Mutations (each run, then restored, then green):

- Generation hook removed (`generate.rs` from `upstream/main`): 4 of 5 `offset` pins red (the door pin stays green, as it must).
- Door refusal removed (`gates.rs`): `the_offset_with_a_taper_or_an_open_run_is_refused_at_the_door` red.
