title: feat(pathkernel): the medial line, trace and helix guide planners
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Sub-PR 2 of 2 for #4176 (K2, the guide stage). Sub-PR 1 (the ring and row planners) merged as PR #4189. This PR adds the medial line, the trace of a chain and the helix guide planners. No old planner changes. No planner calls the new code yet, so with the default switch the output is identical. The baseline pins of the side branch stay green.

## Public surface

- `guide::MedialPlanner`: the medial axis of the cutter-centre area, family `Medial`. Refusals: `NO_MEDIAL`, `NARROW_NECK`, `MEDIAL_TOO_FINE`, `NOT_MEDIAL`.
- `guide::TracePlanner` on the new region kind `KernelRegion::Chains(ChainRegion)`, built by `chain_region(sel, plane, tool, keep_out)`. Refusals: `NOT_A_CHAIN`, `NOT_TRACE`, `TRACE_COLLAPSES`, `TRACE_KEPT_OUT`.
- `TraceOffset`: above zero is to the left of the chain. A closed chain is read counter-clockwise, so its left is its inside.
- `RingsChoice` with a circle: exact circle rings of a hole. Each ring has its `Circle` and a carrier polygon with a chord count from the tolerance (#3756). Refusal: `CIRCLE_NOT_REGION`. `CIRCLE_NOT_YET` is removed.
- `GuideChoice::Helix(HelixChoice)` with `Hand`, and `guide::HelixPlanner`. Refusals: `TOO_MANY_TURNS`, `HELIX_OUTSIDE`, `HELIX_TOO_FINE`, `NOT_HELIX`.
- `Curve::lead()` and `Lead`. `Curve::helix` is the checked constructor (`NOT_ON_HELIX`). `Curve::new` refuses the helix family (`HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD`).
- `Guides` plans each family. `FAMILY_NOT_YET` is removed. The area planners refuse a chain region with `NOT_AN_AREA`.
- New in `camcraft-geometry`, each in its own file:
  - `Region::medial_axis`, `Region::medial_spacing`, `MedialAxis`, `MedialCurve` (`geo2d/medial.rs`, with a crate-private Delaunay in `geo2d/delaunay.rs`);
  - `offset_side` and `SidePiece` (`geo2d/side_offset.rs`).

The guide choices moved from `guide.rs` to `guide/choice.rs` with no change. The public paths stay the same by re-export.

## Pins

- `camcraft-geometry` lib:
  - `geo2d::medial::tests::*` (slot, rectangle, annulus, input order, refusals, a touching neck);
  - `geo2d::delaunay::tests::*` (a co-circular grid, scattered points);
  - `geo2d::side_offset::tests::*`.
- `camcraft-pathkernel` `laws`:
  - `guide_medial`, `guide_trace`, `guide_helix`;
  - `guide_laws`: the medial planner, the circle rings and the helix run through `kit::run` and hold L1 to L4;
  - `guide_trace::the_trace_holds_l1_to_l4`.
- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels::kernel_guides`: agreement with the #4153 goldens of Trace, Engrave, Slot, Circular, Bore and Thread (the guide geometry only). Each difference is named in the file header and in the decisions file.

## Gates on the final head 2e7f78856, base `origin/side/path-kernel` 25f3838db

- `cargo check --tests` for pathkernel, geometry and motion, one at a time: clean.
- Clippy `-D warnings` for geometry, pathkernel and motion: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: the geometry change makes it a full batch plan. Result: 1223 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 88.9 min. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and clippy.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 7 steps, 0 failed.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/4176-kernel-guides-medial-trace-helix.md`. The main decisions:
- The medial line is the theta-pruned Voronoi medial axis. It is not a port of the old single-channel spine.
- A chain region holds the chains of a trace.
- The circle rings use the stepover from the wall. The Bore recipe gives `rc / count` to get the old even rings.
- There is one helix for each choice. The hand is geometry, and the direction of travel stays with stage 4.

## Review fix (head 33c116cfa): later stages keep the data of a family

The review found that the K4 order stage reversed a curve with `Curve::new`, which refuses the helix family. Commit 6aa630fee closes the finding with one rule for the class: a later stage that restarts, reverses or replaces a curve makes it again through the constructor of the curve's family (`Curve::with_points`: `Curve::helix` with the same circle and lead, else `Curve::new` with the same circle), or it refuses by a reason of its own stage.

- Order: a helix always runs down its lead. A reversal also turns it up its lead, so the stage reverses a helix only when the guide set holds it upward. The hand sets the side of the material. A direction that the hand does not give is named by the order note `HELIX_HAND_SETS_DIRECTION`. A failed rebuild is the order reason `NOT_REVERSIBLE`.
- Load (K3): constant engagement inserts passes only before a ring (`NOT_A_RING` else). Trochoidal loops leave a curve with a lead, an exact circle or a changing depth as it is (`SHAPE_KEPT`). A refused rebuild is `SET_NOT_KEPT`. Loops that make no curve are `LOOPS_NOT_A_CURVE`.
- Link and entry make no new curve.
- Pins: `later_stages::each_guide_family_keeps_its_data_or_is_refused_by_the_stage_in_each_later_stage` (7 rows x 13 stage cells) and `later_stages::the_order_stage_runs_a_helix_down_its_lead_and_names_a_direction_that_its_hand_does_not_give`. - Merge of `side/path-kernel` df9ec30b6 (PRs #4265 and #4253) in 7922d0c6c: no conflicts, empty remerge-diff (class SAME).

The quick plan is a full batch (1223 steps) because of geometry. The geometry change is one doc sentence, so the batch was not run again; the full batch ran green on 33c116cfa.

- A trace through all the kernel stages. The entry stage refuses a region that is not an area today. Follow-up #4236.
- Engrave with an avoid item against its golden. The old keep-out comes from an avoid item with its own pad.

body:
## What changed

The Heidenhain DIN/ISO post (`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`) now writes PECK and DEEP holes as the expanded chain in plain `G00` / `G01` blocks. This occurs at each R clearance. The post writes no `G205` and no peck `G200`.

- The old `G205` had `Q257` = `Q202` = the peck and `Q258=0`. The control made a full retract after each infeed, then moved at FMAX to the cut face.
- The old peck `G200` had `Q200=0`. The control moved at FMAX to the last depth.
- The chain makes chip-break hops (PECK), or rapids to R and feeds down from R (DEEP). The simulation and the gouge check read the chain. The posted blocks are now that chain, move for move.
- DRILL and SPOT keep `G200`, with `Q202` = the whole depth (one infeed). Taps keep `G206` / `G207`.

title: fix(app): the stock export judges the mesh as the file holds it; the written-corner weld settles duplicates by edge parity
body:
## What changed

A binary STL writes each corner as f32. Corners closer than one f32 step become one corner in the file, so a stock mesh that passed the closed check in f64 could be written with repeated corners and edges not on two facets.

- `stock_export::file_bytes` (new, `crates/app/src/stock_export.rs`) judges the mesh as the file will hold it: it rounds the corners to their written f32 values (`repair::weld_at_f32`). When a facet collapses at those values, or two distinct corners round to one, it welds bit-exact and checks the result with `unpaired_edges`, refusing by name if the written mesh would not be closed. A mesh with nothing to collapse writes byte for byte as before. `write_stl` and the UI's stock export (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`, same line count) use it.
- In that written-corner weld only, duplicate facets settle by edge parity (`duplicate_sets` with `Duplicates::ByParity`): a set of copies whose edges the rest of the mesh uses an even number of times keeps no copy; otherwise the first copy stays. Keeping one copy of a back-to-back pair left that pair's three edges on one facet each.
- `repair::weld`, which `RepairModel` runs on a part model, keeps main's rule (`Duplicates::KeepFirst`): the first copy of each duplicate set stays. The first version of this PR used parity there too, and review found that it removed double-sided surfaces of a part model (finding 1). The export's input is a closed surface, so a duplicate set there can only be two faces the rounding laid together.

Why parity and not the issue's "k mod 2" (keep a copy when the count is odd): k mod 2 removes a single stray duplicate on a closed solid (k = 2), which the existing pin `drop_degenerate` keeps (a flipped duplicate on a cube stays as one copy). Parity keeps that case as pinned and removes the back-to-back pair the weld leaves.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/4182-stl-as-written.md`.

## Pinning tests

Synthetic shapes only.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs` `the_exported_file_is_closed_as_written_and_a_clean_mesh_writes_unchanged`: on main `e6849c5ae` with only the test added it fails, facets written left `6`, right `4`. On this branch it passes.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs` `two_solids_whose_edges_meet_in_the_file_are_refused`: on head `025f59e36` (no corner-meet check) it fails, the bytes are written. On this branch it is refused by name.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs` `a_sliver_that_collapses_to_nothing_as_written_is_refused`: passes on this branch (refused, "collapses to nothing").
- `crates/geometry/tests/repair.rs` `a_back_to_back_pair_left_at_the_written_corners_goes_and_the_mesh_stays_closed`: through `weld_at_f32`, the thin tetrahedron gives (triangles after, dropped) `(0, 4)` and no open edge. With one copy kept, it was `(1, 3)` and open (the reviewer's mutation M1 on `025f59e36`).
- `crates/geometry/tests/repair.rs` `corners_closer_than_an_f32_step_weld_at_their_written_values`: passes on this branch.
- `crates/app/tests/repair_model.rs` `a_double_sided_sheet_keeps_its_facets_through_repair` and `a_double_sided_fin_on_a_cube_stays_through_repair` (finding 1): on `025f59e36`'s repair both fail. The sheet is refused ("would update the model to empty geometry"), and the fin cube drops 4 facets, where 2 is expected. On this branch both pass.

On this branch: repair 12 tests, repair_model 7, stock_export 5, all pass.

On head `217de3194` (base upstream/main `1c0152c91`):

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: feat(tools)!: component library store and project persistence
body:
Stacked on #4201. This PR adds three commits on top of it: `8fd0a47ec..745234df7`.

## What changed

This is slice 1 of #3645.

- **Project file v84.** A `.camproj` now holds the document tool component table (`components`). Each tool can also hold its component stack (`assembly`).
  - The loader reads the table and each stack before any world write.
  - Each link must name a row, and each stack must resolve (the #3643 resolver). If not, the file is refused by the tool name or the component id.
  - The loader lands the rows and stacks through `table_set` and `set_assembly`. This replaces the clear-on-open line of #4201.
  - The derived `ToolDef` and `ToolBody` stay as the file states them, so an open does not change a posted program.
  - An assembled body gets its source and the judged resolver bands back when its drawn outline is the outline that the stack resolves to (`assembly_wire::as_derived`).
- **One wire form for a component row** (`project::component_wire`), for the project and the library. The codes are written as text: the ISO 1832 insert code, the connection codes, and the ISO 5608 seat letters. The geometry holds the port frames, the body, the cutting point and the bore stops. Each record is read strictly: an unknown key is refused, each row is built again through the checked constructors, and each refusal names the row.
- **`library_ref { id, content_hash }`** on a document row. The hash is FNV-1a 64 over the wire JSON of the name, the item and the geometry.
- **User component library** (`component_library`, `component_library::store`):
  - The file format is `camcraft-components/1` with `units: "mm"`.
  - The folder is `CAMCRAFT_COMPONENTS` (an absolute path). If it is not set, the folder is `<platform data dir>/camcraft/components`. The file is `components.camcomponents`.
  - A save writes a temp file, then renames it.
  - The read is all or nothing. The holder library (each entry with a taper) and the starter tool catalog are read-only built-ins in the `builtin:` id space.
- **Sync.** `sync_status` returns `NotLinked`, `UpToDate`, `UpdateAvailable` or `MissingFromLibrary`. It never applies a library copy.
  - `SyncDocumentComponent` (undoable) puts the library copy into the row, records the link, and derives each user tool again in one undo step through the `EditDocumentComponent` law (`with_row`).
  - A hand edit keeps the link.
  - A change of the link alone derives no tool again.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3645-component-library.md`.

## Compatibility

- `PROJECT_VERSION` goes from 83 to 84. Each file that this build writes says v84, so a v83 build refuses it and cannot drop the table. Files of v83 and older open unchanged. This includes #2016 / PR #2092 `holder` references. The commit is `feat(tools)!:` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, as for the v82 and v83 steps and as the issue asks.
- The `.camtools` format does not change in this PR.

## Readings

- The round trip is byte-stable. The project has six component rows and three assembled tools: two indexable cutters with a shared insert, and one solid end mill in an adapter in a holder (two bodies united band by band).

title: fix(post): refuse a preset above the machine's last preset row
body:
Stacked on #4164 (merge #4164 first).

## What changed

- A machine file can state a new optional key, `controller.work_offset_max`. It is the highest work offset that the control holds. On a Heidenhain control it is the last row of the preset table.
- The machine reader and the raw post engine refuse a value that is not a whole number from 1 to 255. The message names the key.
- The key is an installation fact, the same as `tooling.max_tool_number` (#4164). The mirror carries it.
- The post engine refuses a `PARAM WorkOffset` above the key. The refusal names the setup and the key. It comes before any script hook runs, so it applies to each post.
- `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` states `"work_offset_max": 5`. Its description tells the shop to check the preset table at the control.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- A machine without the key keeps the post's own limit. A key above the post's own limit does not raise that limit.

## Cause

- Both Heidenhain posts accept presets 1..6 (`workOffsetMax = 6`).
- The Picomax preset table on the 2008 delivery CD (`PRESET.PR`) has rows 0..5 only (`docs/research/heidenhain/picomax-55-review.md`, defect 14).
- `Q339=+6` names a row that does not exist. The control stops with an alarm.
- The machine file had no place to state the row count.

The refusal is a hard error, not a counted warning. A counted warning was not enough: the Klartext post throws "missing or unsupported preset (WorkOffset)" when the engine holds back the offset, and that error hid the warning.

## Tests

Pins, in the `heidenhain_cycles` directory suite (new submodule `heidenhain_cycles/preset_rows.rs`, no new test binary):

- `preset_rows::heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_preset_above_the_machine_preset_table`: preset 5 posts with no warning, and preset 6 is refused with `setup Setup1: uses work offset 6` and `controller.work_offset_max`. It runs both posts on the raw file and on the parsed mirror.
- `preset_rows::an_unstated_or_larger_machine_maximum_keeps_the_post_limit`: no machine posts preset 6; a key of 99 posts preset 6 and refuses 7 with "work offsets 1-6 only".
- `preset_rows::a_malformed_work_offset_max_is_refused_by_name`: 0, -1, 2.5, "5" and 256 are refused by the reader and by the raw engine.

Red before the fix: yes. On the unchanged code the test did not compile (no `Machine::work_offset_max`). With the two field assertions taken out, all three tests failed: preset 6 posted, and no value was refused.

Mutations (each one red, then restored and green):

- Engine guard disabled: `heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_preset_above_the_machine_preset_table` red.
- Mirror line disabled: the same test red (mirrored input).
- Reader range widened to 256: `a_malformed_work_offset_max_is_refused_by_name` red.

Gate on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `9d6ebbd62`: 343 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan included each app suite that reads `heidenhain.cps`, `klartext_builtin`, `machine_controller` and the example catalog suites.
- Then a clippy fix (`b3541f715`, the guard as one `if let`). `cargo xtask gate quick --base HEAD~1` on the final head: 13 steps, 0 failed. It ran `post suites: lib`, `work_offset_index`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and the first-part suites.
- `cargo xtask gate test preset_rows --crate post --binary heidenhain_cycles` on the final head: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane was not run. Its dry run shows only the motion adaptive and pocket twins. This diff does not change them.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suites and the quick plan ran green. `git diff --stat` against #4164's head shows no `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` change.

## Not exercised

- The row count was not checked at the control. The value 5 comes from the 2008 CD. The issue's first "Done means" item stays with the maintainer. If the shop added rows, raise the key in the machine file.
- The setup's work offset list in the UI still offers offsets up to the post's limit. The post refusal blocks the wrong program. Display is a possible follow-up.
- An older app reads a project from this build and drops the key (no `deny_unknown_fields` on `Machine`), so it keeps the post's own limit. This is the same as for #4164.
- No UI change, so no screenshots.
- No heavy step: this is a `P3` PR (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

## Overlaps

- #4164: same lines (`FACT_KEYS`, the `Machine` fields, `parse_mch_with`, `checked_input`, `mirror`). This PR is stacked on it.
- #4161: touches `def.rs`, `parse.rs` and `machine_installation.rs`, in other fields and functions. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3982: touches `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, another section. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Opening the project clears the acknowledgment and keeps the raw-stock-only mark. The MCP tool `set_raw_stock_only` exposes the optional acknowledgment (`report_inherited_deficits`).

### Review fixes (`3c4e3b7b8`)

Two independent reviews of the first version found six cases. Each case has a pinning test that fails without its fix.

- A program of touch probes only plans nothing in the column simulation (#108). It was refused even with the acknowledgment. Now it is judged and noted the same way.
- A torch or a wire removes material that the column never sees (#670). An undercut pass lowers no column top (#1444). A program with one of these keeps the full gate, because unchanged tops cannot show that the program left a cell alone.
- A probe in a setup other than the judged one never uses that setup's acknowledgment.
- A program that cuts nothing was judged on the first setup's stock, wherever it ran. Now `carry::walk` takes its steps from the program's own operations when nothing is planned. The program is judged on the setup it runs in and crosses setups by the same entry law as a cutting program. Cutting programs walk exactly as before. **This changes the ordinary verdict (acknowledgment off) for programs of probes or torches only.**
- Across setups that the walk cannot cross (a later setup's model stock, a machine change), such a program now refuses by name in the not-judged arm. Before, it posted. The operations' generator verdicts judge paths, not stock.

## Readings

The synthetic fixture has a step 5 mm below the part surface. Posting holds before acknowledgment, passes with a located 5.00 mm note after acknowledgment, and holds again after reopening. A second cut that deepens the step by 3 mm still holds posting. A probe-only program behaves the same way on the stock of its own setup. A torch, a T-slot pass, or a probe in another setup keeps the hold. A two-setup probe or plasma program that the walk cannot cross is refused, and no NC file is written.

## Checks

- On `3c4e3b7b8`, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed 353 of 354 steps, with 0 stalled. The one failure was the golden comparison in `sinumerik_810m_post`. It read a stale CRLF working copy of the committed kit file `docs/tester-kits/sinumerik-810m-vmc200/air_cut_vmc200.mpf`, which is marked `eol=lf` and is not changed by this PR. After the copy was restored to the committed bytes (no diff), that suite passed 3 of 3.
- Clippy passed for all targets of `camcraft-app` with warnings denied.
- The 16 pinning tests are in the `keep_law` binary under `incoming_stock_deficits`. Twenty other suites on posting, probing, plasma and setups also passed: 179 of 179 tests in 21 suites on `3c4e3b7b8`.

The test setup uses synthetic stock on Windows. The light lane belongs to the independent upstream review. Full heavy lanes run at the release cut.

The fork synced at v0.26.0.

## Notes

`3c4e3b7b8` also updates the `set_raw_stock_only` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` (the new `report_inherited_deficits` parameter). This PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

A waterjet-only program across setups is refused by the same not-judged arm. Its refusal line names probes and torches rather than the waterjet. The post is still refused; only the wording is general.

Process change: yes

Effort: high

Changelog: Report acknowledged incoming-stock deficits that the program leaves at their incoming heights; judge a probe- or torch-only program on the setup it runs in.

title: fix(multiaxis): start and exit picks for the multi-axis contour
body:
## What changed

The Multi-Axis Contour (`OpType::MultiAxisContour`, the drive-curve planner `multiaxis::contour_curve`) takes a start point and an exit point. This is slice 2 of #3330. Slice 1 (the 5-Axis Contour) is PR #4006.

The title uses `fix`: the issue has the `bug` label, and PR #4028 used `fix` for the same reason.

Behaviour (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve_seam.rs`, hook in `contour_curve_seamed`):

- Each pick acts on the drive curve nearest it. The other curves keep their automatic cut. The cut order of the curves does not change.
- A pick with a Z is read in 3D. A pick without a Z is read in XY.
- Closed curve, start: the curve starts at its point nearest the pick. A foot between two vertices becomes a new vertex on that segment.
- Closed curve, exit: the curve cuts its full lap from its seam. Then it runs on along its own points to its point nearest the exit pick, and the tool leaves there.
- Open curve: the start pick selects the end where the cut starts (the nearer end). The exit pick selects the end where the cut leaves. The direction of the curve can reverse.
- The re-sequence occurs before the walk. Thus the rest law, the tilt limit (`command_axis` in the max-tilt cone) and the shank dodge judge each station of the picked path, as on the automatic path. The app's centre-cut audit (`audit_posed`) and the verify pass also read the picked path.
- The kind has no leads, so there is no lead-room law.
- With no pick, `apply` returns before it touches the curves. The path is byte-identical.
- `PickCapability::Ring` for the kind. The MCP `edit_operation` schema says how the kind reads a pick.

## Refusals (by name, before any motion)

- `start point (x, y): the nearest drive curve stands D mm away, farther than R mm (1.5 tool diameters) - ...` (also for the exit).
- `start point (...): drive curve N is open and its cut can start only at an end; its nearest end (...) stands D mm away, farther than R mm - ...` (also for the exit: `leave only at an end`).
- `exit point (...): it is nearer the end of open drive curve N where the start point begins the cut - ...`.
- `start point (...): the plunge column over drive curve N at (x, y, z) crosses the part - ...` and `exit point (...): the retract column over drive curve N at (...) crosses the part - ...`. The column law sweeps the ball up the vertical line to the hop plane, every 0.25 mm, and it checks the shank at each step when shank avoidance is on.

## Mutations

Each mutation was applied alone, the pins were run, and the source was restored.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `curve_seam::rotate` keeps the automatic seam (start seat off) | RED: `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | `run_on`: the full lap dropped (the exit becomes a chord) | RED: `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick` |
| M3 | the plunge column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | the retract column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | open curve: the start reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`; app: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| M6 | open curve: the exit reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends` |
| M7 | the same-end exit refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M8 | the open start end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M9 | the open exit end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | the curve reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | the column sweep reads only the station (no samples up the column) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| A1 | the app arm passes an empty seam | RED: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| A3 | the kind's capability back to `PICK_OWED` | RED: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` |

## Readings

- The pins that say "the cut geometry does not change" sample each cut move every 0.25 mm in both directions. Each sample of the picked path must be within 0.02 mm of the automatic ball-centre path (no chord, no gouge). Each sample of the automatic path must be within 0.02 mm of the picked path (no part of the curve left uncut). The walk's chord budget is 0.0025 mm.
- Box 40 x 40 x 15, ring at z = 7.5, ball r = 3: the start pick (20, -1) gives a first ball centre at (20.0, -3.0, 7.5) within 0.05 mm. The exit pick (-1, 20) gives a last ball centre at (-3.0, 20.0, 7.5).
- A canopy slab at z 18 to 20 above the middle of the y = 0 wall: a pick under it is refused for the plunge and for the retract. A pick on the x = 0 wall cuts.

## Pinning tests

- motion `multiaxis` (module `curve_seam`): `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_path_byte_for_byte`.
- app `start_exit_shared` (module `multiaxis_contour`): `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `undo`, `redo`); and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated).
- No new top-level test binary: the new files are modules of `multiaxis` and `start_exit_shared`.

## Goldens moved

None expected. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A pick on a shank-avoid path where the shank, not the ball, blocks the column. The shank step uses the existing `shank_hits_at`; no pin drives it.
- A closed drive curve through the application (the app pins use the box's four open top edges). The closed curve is pinned at motion scale.
- A setup with a rotated frame: the picks and the drive curves are both in the setup frame, as for the 5-Axis Contour.

## Code shape

- `curve.rs` had 860 lines. Its unit tests moved, unchanged, to `curve_tests.rs`. It now has 719 lines, with the hook. A further split is a follow-up.
- No new crate edge.

## Remaining kinds of #3330

Parallel5D, Swarf, AdvancedSwarf, RotaryContour, RotaryParallel, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Flow5D.

## Gate

All on head `8d61b24d9` (local Mac):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 216 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: multiaxis`, `motion suites: pivot5d`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy step: none (P2).

Decision: `docs/decisions/3330-multiaxis-contour-picks.md`.

Effort: max.

Changelog: The Multi-Axis Contour takes a start point and an exit point: each pick re-sequences the drive curve nearest it, and an impossible pick is refused by name.

title: fix(adaptive): a 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point
body:
## What changed

The 2D Adaptive (`Adaptive2D`) takes a start point and an exit point (slice of #1448). The picks are the shared operation-level `picks` field of #3339. The command, the project file, the stamp and MCP `edit_operation` need no change.

- `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`: `Adaptive2D` is now `PickCapability::Region`. Only the Adaptive2D arm changes. The door refusal of the settings that cannot hold a pick is added to `pick_refusal`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_picks.rs` (new): the door (`adaptive_pick_refusal`), the picked entry, the piece order, the refusals, and the exit run back on the posted path (`exit_on_path`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm.rs`: `choose_entry` uses the start point as the seed. The pieces are ordered by `order_pieces`. A picked plan that falls back to the rings, or that keeps an overload, is refused by name. The budget unit test moves to `pocket_hsm_ring.rs` (the same test, so that the file stays under 400 lines).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`: one hook after `emit_pocket_passes` for the exit.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_avoid.rs`: a pick in a "Do not touch" keep-out is refused with the item names.
- `crates/motion/src/approach.rs`: two runtime fields, `start_point` and `exit_point`. They are not saved. `crates/app/src/operation/adaptive_pick_op.rs` (new) lays the op's picks over the generation copy, or refuses them.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wcs_yaw.rs`: under a Z-rotated work offset the Adaptive picks turn into the generation frame, as the Slot picks do.
- UI: the Lead in / Lead out tab of the 2D Adaptive draws the Start point and Exit point groups (`start_exit_rows::region_groups`, drawn from `op_page.rs` because `mill2d_page.rs` is already over 400 lines). The viewport pick and the marks take the 2D Adaptive.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3327-adaptive-start-exit.md`.

## The law

- Start: the start point is the seed of the HSM plan. The helix (or the plunge) goes down there on each level, through the same entry law and the same triangle room as the automatic seed. The planner then grows the cleared area from that bore and measures each cut on its stock.
- Exit: the last pass of each level ends where the plan ends, on its closing ride along the walls. Then the tool runs back along the same posted moves in reverse (one round of the outer wall at most) to the point nearest the exit point, and climbs out there. A reversed line is the same line and a reversed arc is the same arc, so the run back cuts no new material and makes no feed-feed crossing. The piece nearest the exit point is cut last.
- The cut geometry does not change otherwise. Without a pick no new code runs.

## Refusals (by name, the pick is never moved, nothing is cut)

- `the start point (x, y) is outside the area the tool centre can reach ...`
- `the helix of radius r has no room at the start point (x, y) - the tool centre has c mm of room there and the helix needs n ...` (the plan's own 0.6 helix share)
- `the start|exit point (x, y) is inside the 'Do not touch' keep-out of <names> ...`
- `the exit point (x, y) is d mm from the closing ride of the last pass along the walls - the most is L ...` (L = 1.5 tool diameters + stock to leave, the contour's reach law)
- `the exit point ... is at the piece of the area where the cut starts, and n other piece(s) are cut after it ...`
- `an exit point needs the tool to climb out after the last pass of each level ...` (a level link that stays down)
- `the plan from the start point does not hold the optimal load (<planner note>) ...`
- `the HSM plan <reason> - the Offset rings or the trochoid that would cut the area instead do not take a start or exit point ...`
- At the door and at generation: a tilted (3+2) op, the Trochoidal method, Pass starts at Inside or Outside, a rest pass, and a start point with a Ramp or Arc entry.

## Readings

On a rectangle 60 x 40, tool D10, helix R2 (motion fixture):

- Automatic seed (30, 20): widest cut on the shape-mask meter 1.62 mm. Start point (15, 12): 1.79 mm. The limit in the test is 2.03 mm (the optimal load step with the plan's margin and the grid's).
- Start points (20, 15), (25, 20), (15, 12) are taken. A start point at (40, 25) makes the spiral keep "the least overload": it is refused. A start point at (12, 12) makes the plan cross itself: it is refused with that reason.
- Exit point (58, 20): each level ends at (55, 20). `crossed_pairs` is empty. The first try (a run back on the planner's walk, before the arc fit) read two crossings between the two arc fits, so the run back is made on the posted moves.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels` (`adaptive_picks` module):
  - `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` (two levels, no overload note, no crossing, widest cut under the limit)
  - `the_exit_point_is_where_the_last_pass_ends_on_each_level` (two levels, no crossing)
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `camcraft-app` `start_exit_shared` (`adaptive` module):
  - `the_entry_is_at_the_start_point_and_the_last_pass_ends_at_the_exit_point` (golden CL `adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`)
  - `the_picks_hold_under_a_90_degree_wcs_yaw`
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name_and_nothing_is_cut` (also the door: tilt, Trochoidal, Pass starts at Inside, Ramp entry)
  - `the_picks_ride_the_command_undo_the_file_and_the_stamp` (undo restores the previous path to the move; no pick plans the earlier path to the move)
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_adaptive_picks` (`edit_operation`, `get_job` reads them back, `undo` clears them, `list_operation_types` says `start: true, exit: true`)
  - `the_2d_adaptive_takes_a_start_and_an_exit_point`, and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated)
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `the_2d_adaptive_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_and_takes_an_exit`, `a_2d_adaptive_takes_the_viewport_pick_and_shows_its_marks`

New test files join existing suites (`pass_start_levels/`, `start_exit_shared/`). No new top-level test binary.

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`. A path without a pick runs no new code (see the gate: `golden_cl`, the example catalog suites).

## Not exercised

- The keep-out refusal has no pinning fixture. The code is one `contains` test on the keep-out region that `adaptive_spiral_avoid_on` already builds.
- The "climb out" refusal (a level link that stays down) and the "exit at the start's piece" refusal have no fixture.
- A plunge entry at a start point is taken by the door. Its first turn out of a tool-size bore is the planner's existing note, not an overload refusal; no fixture.
- The Trochoidal method stays refused (its seed is on the medial line). #3932 (the trochoidal entry slots to a wall) is a separate path; this PR does not change it.
- No machine run.

## Why `fix`

The issue is labelled `bug` (the 2D Adaptive refused a start and an exit point that #1448 says it takes), and the earlier slice of the same family (#3325, the Slot) shipped as `fix(slot)`. So this PR is a `fix` too, and it merges when it is reviewed.

## Gate

All on the final head `3764e7ed9` (the branch with `origin/main` merged in; one conflict in `start_exit_shared.rs`, where #3981 and this PR each added lines to the gate map and to one assertion; both kept), local Mac, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 875 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (83.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `golden_cl`, `ui suites: lib`, and the example catalog suites by name: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the code head before the merge of main (the merge changed only test lines in `start_exit_shared.rs`).

Note: under load, the quick gate marked `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` slow (>60 s with 8 test threads) in the first run, not in the final run. The test plans one 60 x 40 area on two levels.

Heavy step: none. This is a P2 issue, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a targeted heavy step only to a P1 PR under the safety floor.

Changelog: The 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point: the entry goes down at the start point and the cleared area grows from there, and the last pass of each level runs back along its closing ride to the point nearest the exit point; a point that the plan cannot hold is refused by name.

title: fix(tools,sim,ui): read corner_r for dovetail cutters
body:
## What changed

Dovetail cutters (`ToolKind::Dovetail`) now read `corner_r` across geometry, verification, stock simulation, and the UI:

- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `Head::Dove` stores `{ cot, corner_r }`. `Undercut::rho` evaluates the corner arc up to `s_tan = c * (1 + sin t)` and the tangent flank above `s_tan`. `Undercut::contact()` returns `(r, corner_r)`.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `undercut::refusal` checks `corner_r` in `[0, diameter / 2]`, `s_tan <= flute_len + NECK_MEETS`, and neck clearance against the rounded flank.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs` and `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`: `head_outline` and `Tool::meridian` emit the rounded corner arc and straight flank.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/`: `Cutter::atoms` emits `Prof::Zone` (`[0, s_tan]`) and `Prof::Dove` (`[s_tan, flute_len]`), or one `Prof::Zone` when the flank top meets `s_tan`. `swept::rho_expanded` and `rotary_geom::shapes` handle `Prof::Zone`. `Frame` moves to `probe_frame.rs` under the 400-line rule.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/`: `SdfTool::Dovetail` and `RevKind::Dove` add `corner: f64`. `field_dove::dove_dist` computes the exact Euclidean SDF of the rounded dovetail head.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`: `tool_settings_grid`, `tool_summary`, `tool_cutter_params`, and `tool_undercut_row::seed` show and preserve `Corner radius` for `ToolKind::Dovetail`, while keeping it hidden and zeroed for `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, and `Lollipop`.
- `docs/decisions/4004-dovetail-corner-radius.md`: records the unattended design decisions.

## Readings

For the `#4004` dovetail cutter (`diameter = 19.05 mm`, `tip_angle = 60 deg`, `flute_len = 9.525 mm`, `shank_d = 8.0 mm`):

- `corner_r = 0.0 mm`: top radius is `4.026 mm` (`contact = (9.525, 0.0)`). The 24 mm wide, 30 deg slot verifies clean and posts.
- `corner_r = 0.254 mm`: top radius is `4.212 mm` (`+0.186 mm` wider; `contact = (9.525, 0.254)`). The 24 mm slot catches `Warning::Gouge` and holds the post.
- `corner_r = 3.0 mm`: top radius is `6.222 mm` (`+2.196 mm` wider; `contact = (9.525, 3.0)`). The 24 mm slot catches `Warning::Gouge` and holds the post, and field stock removes the wider flank and rounded bottom corner.

## Screenshots

Off-screen renders (`egui_kittest`, headless `wgpu`, 1440 x 1100 px) show tool `DT-1905-60` (dovetail, diameter 19.05 mm, flank angle 60 deg, flutes 9.525 mm, shank 8.0 mm, `corner_r = 1.0 mm`) across the three changed UI surfaces.

| Surface | Before (`baad348f1`) | After (`e2f674ee3`) |

| Properties summary | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/49847668c9153a8120102476b27bce0cd29660b2/4009/before-1-properties-summary.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/49847668c9153a8120102476b27bce0cd29660b2/4009/after-1-properties-summary.png) |
| Tool editor (Tool library window) | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/49847668c9153a8120102476b27bce0cd29660b2/4009/before-2-tool-editor.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/49847668c9153a8120102476b27bce0cd29660b2/4009/after-2-tool-editor.png) |
| Draw cutter (Tool shape, Profile tab) | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/49847668c9153a8120102476b27bce0cd29660b2/4009/before-3-draw-cutter.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/49847668c9153a8120102476b27bce0cd29660b2/4009/after-3-draw-cutter.png) |

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- The Sodick post refuses an open run's skims by name at its rapid
  guard: its manual states no such pass structure, and the generic ISO
  post is the one that cuts, travels and threads anew around each
  boundary.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

Screenshots (images only on the fork's pr-screenshots branch)

- Controls, before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-controls-before.png
- Controls, after (the new Closing overlap row and its help): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-controls-after.png
- Full window, before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-window-before.png
- Full window, after: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-window-after.png

Rework after the safety review (head 795d69e95)

The eight review items of 2026-11-25 are addressed on the same branch:

1. The Centre slit's run-out clearance joins the generation stamp
   (cutting.rs), so an edited or re-stated clearance reads Stale -
   pinned through the edit command and a project reload (wire_stamp).
2. The overlap's ride includes the seam edge's own remainder back to
   the seam: a 100 mm overlap covers exactly 100 mm of arc, forward
   and reversed, and a ride longer than one full lap is refused by
   name (motion tests, both directions, near the perimeter).
3. An open run's skim passes are rethreaded in the air: a travel move
   (a rapid, no wire through it) marks each pass boundary, the wire
   verify judges each pass at its own kerf and its own ends, and the
   generic ISO post cuts, travels and threads anew around it - a new
   app test generates, verifies AND posts an open run with a skim
   (new goldens wire_contour_open_skims.nc and wire_contour_centre_skims.nc).
4. A stated overlap beside a no-core burnout is refused by name at the
   command door (create and edit tested).
5. A stated overlap on a 4-axis cut and beside a constant taper is
   refused by name at the command door (the 3-degree/1 mm case that
   once failed with "repeats a point" now refuses at the door;
   create and edit tested per combination).
6. The three-file merge with current main keeps both sides; the
   resolved tree builds and its gates run (below).
7. Before / after screenshots of the changed Wire Contour controls
   are on the fork's pr-screenshots branch and linked below.
8. This PR edits .claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md; the body
   carries the process line. PROCESS_VERSION is untouched.

The choice per item is recorded in
docs/decisions/3216-wire-overlap-rework.md: items 2 and 3 are defects
of what the feature claims, so they are implemented properly; items 4
and 5 are refused by name at the command door, safer than a
half-implemented overlap on the burnout, 4-axis and taper builders.

Main moved while the rework ran (the wire exit pick, the arc joins, the rotary stated axis, the tool preview), so the branch carries one more merge of current main, resolved keeping both sides, and the gates below ran on the refreshed head.

Gates on the resolved tree: motion lib 668 passed, sim lib 253 passed, app lib 311 passed, ui lib 1659 passed; mcp_wire_contour 8, wire_verify 3, golden_cl 34, wire_post 13, wire_stamp 8, wire_contour 19, wire_burnout 4, wire_taper 11, wire_4axis 8, wire_verify_tol 4,
conformance 7 (every builtin posts every golden byte exact), the
sodick wire suites, g_edm_post, agie_native; clippy app + motion + sim
+ ui --all-targets -D warnings clean. example_catalog's
2d/drill-overfeed refusal.txt CRLF red is the known environmental
#3628, unrelated to this diff (41 of its steps pass).

Changelog: Wire Contour: a stated closing overlap rides the cut past its seam; a centre-line slit side for open runs; skim passes on open runs re-entered from the air.

Process change: yes

Fixes #3216

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
  - A helix inside the uncut core of a tool that is not centre-cutting (review finding on 4bd091166). The core is `plunge_law::CORE` of the tool radius. The wall circle must stand at least that far off the hole axis (`rc >= CORE * r`). The message names the helix radius, the uncut core and the smallest hole that the tool helixes (Ø9 for a Ø6 tool with no leave). A centre-cutting tool keeps the small helix.
- Pass starts at (#3360, from `main`) on a Helical Bore: one helix for each hole has no ring order. Inside and Outside are refused by name at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The Passes tab shows the refusal under the row. Auto is unchanged.
- Bore `entry` (#3828, from `main` by #3832) on a Helical Bore: the helix is the entry of each hole. Plunge, the default, keeps the helix. Ramp and Helix are refused by name (`helical_entry_refusal`), at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The project file and the stamp keep `entry` and `strategy` apart, so a reopened file shows the same refusal.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and on the Lead-in tab main's Entry group, then a hint that the helix is the entry (hover text) and, for a Ramp or Helix entry, a refusal line. The group stays for the helix, so the user can set the entry back to Plunge.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
  - `a_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_of_a_non_centre_cutting_tool_is_refused`: the review's case (Ø6.5, Ø6 tool, 0.4 mm per turn, helix radius 0.25 mm). The NC tool is refused with "1.500 mm uncut core" and "9.000 mm". Ø9 and the issue's Ø11 counterbore still helix with that tool.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_pass_order_by_name`.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_ramp_or_helix_entry_by_name`: Ramp and Helix are refused with "Helical strategy" and the entry name; Plunge keeps the helix.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `a_small_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_is_refused_through_the_operation`: the review's probe through `operation::generate`. The NC tool is refused; the CC tool keeps the small helix with no plunge.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_pass_order_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator both refuse it.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_ramp_or_helix_entry_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator refuse Ramp and Helix; the pair survives the project file; Plunge is not refused; the pass-order refusal is still reached (one Bore arm in `sane.rs`).
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch. `a_helical_bore_keeps_the_entry_group_and_says_the_entry_refusal`: a Ramp entry on the helix shows the refusal line and keeps the Entry combo; Plunge clears the line.
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::a_helical_bore_says_the_pass_start_refusal` (ui lib): Rings take the order; Helical shows the refusal line.

## Gates

Final head 064549362: a merge of `upstream/main` at 498382c8e (no rebase, no force-push). It has hand edits, so it is a DELTA (`git show --remerge-diff 064549362`).

Conflicts with #3832 (Bore entry), both sides kept:
- `crates/app/src/operation/params/holes.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`: the Bore destructure has `strategy`, `pass_start`, `entry` and `picks: _`.
- `holes_page.rs` Lead-in tab: main's `lead_page::bore_entry_group`, then the helical hint and the entry refusal line.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`: `mod bore_strategy;` and `mod bore_entry_group;`.

Hand edits where git merged without a conflict:
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs`: the merge gave two `OpParams::Bore` arms. Main's entry arm came first and hid the helical pass-start arm of this branch. They are one arm now: the entry word, then the pass order, then the helical entry.
- `crates/motion/tests/bore_ramp_angle.rs` (from `main`): `strategy: Default::default()` (Rings).
- `crates/app/tests/bore_helical.rs` (this PR): `entry: Default::default()` (Plunge).

title: feat(post): add Hurco WinMax (NC) ISNC post and Hurco VM10i machine
body:
Replaces #2640 with the same Hurco commit (`4cd8bdae2`, cherry-picked unchanged) on a branch straight off `main`. #2640 was stacked on the Grbl post draft #2506, so it could not merge before #2506. This PR does not need it.

## Review fix round on `3b5c4da6e` (head `19b688263b94a680de590634bd1461cfd58f3b5f`)

- Merged `upstream/main` (`afca9b8b1`) with a merge commit (`dff9b3870`). The merge had no conflicts.
- Main added `assets/posts/sodick-ln2w.cps` (#4065). With `hurco-winmax.cps`, the posts directory has 27 shipped text posts. `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` now counts 27 (commit `19b688263`).
  - Pin proof: with the count at 26 the test fails (`left: 27, right: 26`). With 27 it passes.
- No post or golden changed in this round.
- Evidence on `19b688263`:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 862 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (68.1 min).
  - `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed (10.9 min).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo check --tests -p <pkg>`, one package at a time, for `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-app`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-ui`, `camcraft-kernel`, `camcraft-gpu` and `xtask`: all pass.
- Open: the WinMax simulator result of the new kit (review finding 1). The tester has not replied yet.

## Earlier fix round (tester report on #2573 and this PR)

Head: `3b5c4da6e3d4d5476ac570cb1a7ba3d8483bf27d`.

- The tester's WinMax simulator stopped `DRILL1.NC` at `G43 H562`.
- Default output now writes no `G43 H` line. The control takes the tool length from the Tool Setup screen.
- The new option `toolLengthOffset` (default off) writes `G43 H<tool>` after each `T M6`. With the option on, a tool number outside 1..200 is refused by name. Hurco gives the `H` range as `H00` to `H200`. That is the probable cause of the `G43 H562` alarm.
- The new option `retractAlongToolVector` (default off) writes `G00 M140` at the end of each operation. After it, the next X/Y traverse states its Z first.
- The new option `shortestRotaryPath` (default off) writes `M126` after the start line and `M127` before `M30`.
- Tool pre-fetch (`T110 M6`, then `T104`): Hurco confirms the behaviour. It is not added here. Follow-up #4113 gives the two reasons:
  - the post cannot find the next tool, because `programTools` is sorted by number;
  - with "M6 Initiates Tool Change" set to No, a bare `T` word changes the tool at once.
- Merged `upstream/main`. The conflicts were in registry lists only (`posting_files.rs`, `conformance.rs`, `machine.rs`), where both sides added lines. Both sides are kept.
- After the merge, main's #3442 law (`radius_arcs`: `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk`) found a Hurco defect. An inch arc of r=0.001 mm wrote `G03 X0. Y0. I0. J0.`, which a control reads as a full circle. `onCircular` now asks `arcFate` (PRELUDE) first, as the other shipped posts do. The gate run before the fix failed this test, and it passes after the fix. `comment_escape` now counts 26 shipped text posts.
- Merge fallout in the Hurco tests is fixed: `ProgramId.notes`, `OpParams` fields `picks`, `blend_radius`, `chain_overrides`, `corner_relief` and `pass_start`.

## Hurco sources

Each fact is from Hurco's own documents, in our own words.

- **Hurco WinMax Mill NC Programming online help, "Tool and Radius Offsets (G40-G49)"** (support.hurco.com, `.../NC_Programming/Tool_and_Radius_Offsets_(G40-G49).htm`):
  - When the program has no `G43`/`G44` and no `H` word, the control uses the tool length from the Tool Setup screen.
  - A `G43`/`G44` offset overrides the Zero Calibration length of Tool Setup.
  - The `H` offset code range is `H00` to `H200`. `H00` or `G49` cancels the offset.
  - The offset table on that page shows that in `G49` mode the total offset is the Tool Setup Zero Calibration value. Thus the safe start line keeps `G49`.
- **Online help, "Program Functions"** (`.../NC_Programming/Program_Functions.htm`):
  - "M6 Initiates Tool Change": when this parameter is Yes (the default), a `T` word without `M06` pre-fetches the tool. When it is No, a `T` word alone changes the tool.
  - "Change Tool (M06)": the new tool's Tool Setup offsets load at the change.
  - `M126`/`M127`: the shortest rotary angle path traverse, and its cancel.
  - `M140 [L_] [P_]`: a non-modal retract along the tool vector. Without `L`, the tool retracts to the machine limits.
- **Online help, "Miscellaneous Functions - M Codes"** (`.../NC_Programming/Miscellaneous_Functions_-_M_Codes.htm`): the index lists `M31`, `M126`/`M127` and `M140` as current WinMax M codes.
- **Hurco WinMax Mill NC Programming manual, 704-0116-310 (2010)**:
  - page 4-1, "T Codes": a `T` word does not change the tool by itself. It pre-fetches the tool when "M6 Initiates Tool Change" is Yes.
  - page 5-13: `M126`/`M127` work only on the VMX42 SR.
  - page 5-19: `M140` works only on the VMX42 SR.
  - The current online help does not have these two machine limits. The tester's 2019 WinMax uses `G0 M140` after each operation. Thus the two codes are options, default off.
- **Hurco WinMax Mill documentation (2008)**: not cited for this round. No fact in this round comes from it.

## What changed

- Add clean-room built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` in `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps`.
- Add clean-room 3-axis VMC definition `Hurco VM10i` in `assets/machines/hurco-vm10i.mch`.
- Register both entries in `BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`, and `embedded()` in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`.
- Write Hurco WinMax ISNC blocks:
  - the `G20`/`G21` unit block and `O0001`..`O9999`;
  - `G90 G17 G94 G54..G59 G40 G49 G80` and `G54.1 P1`..`P93`;
  - decimal-second `P` dwell on `G04`/`G82`/`G89`;
  - `G84.2`/`G84.3` rigid tapping and `G84` floating tapping;
  - `G68`/`G69` rotation and `G31` probing with `G10 L2`;
  - no `G91.1`, and no `G43 H` by default.
- Opt-in options `toolLengthOffset`, `retractAlongToolVector` and `shortestRotaryPath`, all default off.
- Record design decisions in `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md`.

## Tests

- Pins for this round, in `crates/post/tests/hurco_winmax_metadata.rs`:
  - `hurco_default_writes_no_g43_h_and_no_opt_in_m_codes`: the default writes `T562 M6` and no `G43`, no `H`, no `M126`/`M127`/`M140`.
  - `hurco_tool_length_offset_option_writes_g43_h_and_refuses_out_of_table`: the option writes `G43 H109` and `G43 H4`, and refuses tool 562 by name (`H01..H200`).
  - `hurco_m140_and_m126_options_write_their_blocks`: one `G00 M140` for each operation, `M126` at the start, `M127` before `M30`, and Z before X/Y after `M140` with the same tool (no tool change).
- Mutations. Each pin was RED with the mutation and GREEN when restored:
  - default `toolLengthOffset` forced on: `hurco_default_writes_no_g43_h_and_no_opt_in_m_codes` fails.
  - `H` range guard raised from 200 to 9999: `hurco_tool_length_offset_option_writes_g43_h_and_refuses_out_of_table` fails.
  - `xyUnknown = true` after `M140` removed: `hurco_m140_and_m126_options_write_their_blocks` fails.
- `crates/post/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs`: the multi-op test now asserts no `G43 H` by default. The word allow-list adds `M126`, `M127` and `M140`.
- Suites run on this head:
  - `camcraft-post`: `hurco_winmax_metadata` 4 passed, `hurco_winmax_post` 8 passed, `hurco_winmax_probe` 2 passed, `script_hurco_winmax` 11 passed.
  - `camcraft-app`: `conformance` 7 passed, `hurco_winmax_post`, `machine`, `post_spindle_rule_all` passed.
  - `camcraft-app` example catalog: `example_catalog` 43 passed (4 ignored), `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work` passed.
- Gate and lint on this head:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `3b5c4da6e`: 856 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (64.3 min). The run on the earlier head `df96d22b9` had 2 failures (`comment_escape`, `radius_arcs`). Commit `3b5c4da6e` fixes both.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `3b5c4da6e`: 0 warnings, exit 0.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` on `3b5c4da6e`: 6 steps, 0 failed (6.2 min). The full heavy lanes were not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 71 release steps. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" says that no PR runs the full heavy lanes, and that a `P6` PR gets no heavy step. Those lanes run at the cut.

## Goldens moved

Regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_hurco_winmax` and `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance`.

- Removed the `G43 H<n>` line after each `T<n> M6` (this round's default change):
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/hurco-winmax/`: `contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole` (`.nc`).
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_hurco-winmax.nc`.
  - `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/hurco-winmax/`: `arcs`, `drill_retract`, `extreme_coords`, `full_circle`, `full_circle_raw`, `probe` (`.nc`).
- Also moved by toolpath changes on `main` (the same programs moved for each other dialect on `main`), with the `G43 H` line removed:
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/hurco-winmax/pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island.nc`
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/hurco-winmax/slot_wide_channel_rows.nc`
- No golden of another post changed. No `.cl` and no `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- No WinMax simulator result for this head yet. A new 3-program kit is in a PR comment. It asks the tester to run `DRILL1.NC` again.
- The options `retractAlongToolVector` and `shortestRotaryPath` are not checked on a Hurco control. The VM10i is 3-axis, so `M126`/`M127` have no rotary axis to act on.
- `G43 H` with the option on is not checked on a control.
- No UI change, so no screenshots.

Changelog: Add built-in Hurco WinMax (NC) ISNC 3-axis mill post and Hurco VM10i machine. The post takes the tool length from Tool Setup (no `G43 H`) by default, with opt-in `G43 H`, `M140` and `M126`/`M127`.

Fixes #2573
